1967-08-22.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-08-22.text:
Aug. 22, 1967
Tuesday

Dear Mother + Dad,

It's Tuesday evening and about 5:15 p.m. here. I thought I'd drop you a few lines and let you know how things have been going.

The plane trip out here was all right but it did seem like a long trip anyway.

As I told you on the phone Sunday, most of the day Thursday was spent in classification. I picked Long Beach and San Diego for home ports and Hawaii for overseas. Thursday night I went into San Francisco for a while. Practically all-day Friday I was at the medical building for a physical and shots. I got 4 shots but will get more later on when I get ready to leave here.

That night I had duty, so I stayed here.

I got up about 10 AM Saturday and went into town to the ball game. After the game we went back downtown and went to China Town and Fisherman's Wharf. I rode the cable car back downtown and later came back here.

Sunday morning I had mess cooking and had to get up about 4:30 AM. I was over there till about 11:30 AM then came back to the barracks and called you. I had duty Sunday, so of course I had to stay here. I went to the movie here that afternoon. The rest of the day I slept and just took it easy.

Yesterday I didn't do much of anything. I just loafed around the barracks and went to the library later on. That evening I went into San Francisco and went to a show. By the time it was over it was rather late so I came back here.

Today was much the same as yesterday. I usually go over to the Exchange three or four times a day for a cup of coffee to occupy some of my time.

Well, Bill is probably on his way to St. Louis now. I hope he sold his car and got what he wanted for it.

There's not much to do around here during the day. Some of the guys get put on working parties but that usually doesn't amount to much. So far I've been able to avoid any of this manual labor!

I'm in the duty section today so that means I have to stay here tonight. I'm going to wash my clothes tonight and go to the show at 8 PM.

I'd like for you to send me some of my civilian clothes if you will. I'd like that brown pair of pants that I wear (Levi's permanent press) with the black wide belt. Send the light-colored permanent press shirt along with the paisley one.

Send my shoes along with a pair of my green socks and a pair of the dark brown ones. I'd appreciate it also if you would send my little radio. Don't get any batteries because I can get them cheaper here. Of course if my ring is back, send it also. Thanks.

The temperature is usually around the 60's here. We wear our blues all the time which came as a surprise to me.

You might check with the reserve center — later on, no hurry, and see if I made third class. Tell them not to notify me here but to wait till I get on board ship, or they can use their own judgement and do what they think is best.

Its not too bad here. This place is nothing like Great Lakes though. It's a lot smaller and its not as strict. I don't know when I get paid while I'm here. I have heard that after you are here 10 days you get your first pay.

Tell everyone I said, Hi. I'll probably write next week or sometime later. There isn't really much to write about because there is not much happening here.

I hope everyone is fine and am sure David is anxious to go back to school. Write if you have the chance.

Your son,
Mike

1967-08-30.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-08-30.text:
Aug. 30, 1967
4:30 PM
Wed.

Dear Mother + Dad,

How is everyone at home? I am getting along fine but anxious to find out when I'll be leaving here.

I got your letter of last Friday yesterday. I received the package this afternoon. Thanks a lot.

I was very glad and surprized to hear that I passed the test for third class. I'll be looking for some kind of notice from them in the next few days.

Do you remember my writing the last time that I usually didn't have to do any work on working parties or anything like that? Well the past three days that I've had duty (Sat., Mon, today) I have had mess cooking. I usually put in about 10 hours each day when I get stuck with that. It's not really bad, just a long time on your feet. We just fix the food and get it ready to be served. We don't have to do dishes or wipe off tables, fortunately. Usually they try to break it up so that you don't have mess duty every day you have duty, but there isn't many men in our barracks so that means you have to do it more often. Actually, I'd rather do that than cleaning up the barracks. It does make the day go faster for me.

Last Wednesday when I came back to the barracks about 3 PM, I found a note laying on my rack. It was from this guy who I palled around at Great Lakes last winter. He had seen my name on a list at his barracks and decided to look me up. He had just got here that day. We were really surprized that we both would be here about the same time. So, we have been going into 'Frisco when we have the chance.

Sunday we went there and spent most of the day. We went to Fisherman's Wharf then went to the Haight/Ashbury section and paid a visit to the "hippies." There are a few of them downtown but if you want to see a lot of them you have to go there. I wish I had a camera with me that day. They lay in the grass in the parks and sleep (among other things), hold public speeches in the parks, paint pictures on the sidewalk! Some of them walk around with a little kitten tied to a string and crawling across their shoulders. There are a lot of tourists that go out there and this makes it easier for the hippies to get publicity and attention.

I haven't heard anything from Bill yet, have you? He probably wishes that he had thought things over a little better before he signed the papers and raised his right hand, but he'll get over it soon, no doubt about that.

I am glad to have my ring back. That new set looks real good. I'll try to take better care of it now that I know the set breaks so easily.

I hope the weather was good for your trip to Effingham. Did David have as much fun this time as he did last time?

I think I am going to buy me a movie camera or do you think a still camera would be best. Just in case I do get one, what size projector do we have 8mm or 16mm? I'd like to take a lot of pictures to remember the places I've been and the things I've seen and will be seeing.

These two weeks have went by fast for me, although it seems that I've been here longer. I should be finding out in the next week or so where I'm going and when.

That's about all I have to say for now. I'll try to write next week. Bye,

Your son,
Mike

P.S.
I noticed you didn't send my radio. That's alright because a lot of the other guys have radios, so I really don't need mine so don't send it in case you remembered you forgot it.

1967-09-06.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-09-06.text:
Wed. 6 Sept. 1967
3 PM.

Dear Mother & Dad,

I got your letter yesterday morning along with one from Bill. I have enclosed his address just in case you haven't heard from him by now. He only wrote one page and explained that he didn't have much to time to write.

Today is the David's birthday, or is it tomorrow, haha. He should have got a card from me, I mailed it Saturday morning.

I got paid for the first time yesterday and cleared $92.00 for the twenty days I was here.

I have been here exactly three weeks today. This morning I was put on assingment. I got the USS JOUETT (DLG-29) out of San Diego. DLG stands for guided missle frigate. I went to the library and found out a little about it;

they finished building it on Dec 3, 1966
cruises at 34 knots
has a crew of 400
547' long, 54' wide and
sets 19.5' out of the water
has [redacted] anti-submarine rockets and torpedoes
1 - 5" gun mount
2 - 3" gun mounts

So, it sounds like a good ship, especially since its not even a year old yet. The living conditions will probably be pretty good. I don't know when I am to report to it, but expect to be out of here in another week.

I think I may buy an instamatic camera. I saw some at the Exchange for $14.50, but I may be able to get a cheaper one in San Francisco.

Yes, I did find the radio when I took the socks out of my shoes to shine them.

Saturday, this buddy of mine from G.L. and I went across the bay and saw the carrier Enterprise. It has been back from Viet Nam for about four weeks and is going back out when it gets some more planes. Its neuclear powered and the biggest ship in the Navy. Let me tell you it is really big. It doesn't seem like your on a ship when you walk around on it.

This Friday night or Sunday, I'm going to the ball game and watch the Cubs play the Giants, providing I'm still here.

When my Reserve check comes, just put it in my checking account and write it down in the account book which is in the dresser drawer.

I haven't heard anything yet about being advanced to third-class. I checked my service record today and there was nothing there in regards to it. The way they run things at the reserve center, it probably won't be official and I'll have to take the test again in the fleet. I wouldn't be suprized at what happens.

I had mess-cooking last night from 4 PM to 12 midnight, but they let us go at about 9:30.

I'll enclose my new address when that I have once I get on the ship. I'll try to let you know some way when I know that I'll be leaving here.

MICHAEL F. DUCY FTGSN 796 16 12
USS JOUETT (DLG-29)
F.P.O.
SAN FRANCISCO, CALIF.
ZIP--?

Its going on 4 o'clock and about time for muster. I'll go over and eat supper after that then probably go into Frisco.

I suggest that you don't write anymore because by the time you get this letter, then get a return letter from you, I'll most likely be gone, and I doubt if they forward any mail. Just wait till you hear from me.

I'll let you know when I leave, bye for now.

your son
Mike

1967-10-05.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-10-05.text:
Thursday Oct. 5, 1967
Bremerton, Washington

Dear Mother And Dad,

It's about 10/30 pm now so I'll try to type out a quick letter. I would write tomorrow or over the weekend but we are suppose to go out to sea till Sunday evening.

I like it real well here on the ship. We have some real great guys in our division and the work is not too hard. I do have trouble finding things to do in the evening though. I usually pass some of my time writing letters one night a week. They do show a movie here on the ship every night but they aren't the greatest. Tomorrow morning I am going to put in for some electronics correspondence courses to give me something to do in my spare time. I really don't want to go on liberty every night because there isn't that much to do around here. And anyway I'd rather save as much money as I can and the best way to do it is to stay on board the ship.

I have enclosed $80.00 to have you put in my checking account. I still have one check for $20.00 that I am going to keep just in case something comes up. I also have about $35.00 in cash so that ought to last till the next pay day. We got paid today and the next one is on the 19th. of this month. I'll send home some more then.

We had a Capitian's inspection Tuesday. I got a very good rating but the division got a good bucause some of the guys were not up to par.

My last letter I wrote I think I said that I was in Seattle. Actually, we are about an hour away from Seattle by ferry. That's one bad thing, if you wan to go over there it takes so long and it costs $170 for a round trip.

The weather has been rather bad for about the past week. We have had a lot of rain and it is rather cool.

I watched part of Wedensday's World Series Game on TV and listened to most of it on the radio today. I think the Cardinals will winx it. At least that's the way Harry Kary figures it will end up so I can't be too wrong.

We went out to sea Friday and came back Saturday evening, earlier than we expected. We were suppose to come back Sunday evening but they had something happen to one of the boilers so we had to return here. We'll be going out again this weekend.

I got the letter you wrote Monday, the 25th. of Sept. Monday of this week.

I think that your job isn't the kind which it is really necessary to put in that after hours time in at meetings and whatever. I agree that what you do on your own time is your own business.

More than likely, next summer I will be returning from the Wes Pac cruise and have 30 days leave coming. Bill will probably have his leave come up about the same time. We could spend part of it here on the coast if you want to come out then we could go home for the rest of it. That's a long way off but I am sure we will be able to figure something out.

Sunday I didn't do much either. I stayed on board and watched the baseball game and the football game on TV. It rained all day then just like the rest of the week.

I got a letter from grandma and she said that she sent Bill a piece out of the paper and she was afraid that he would get in trouble for having it. I'm sure that he would got rid of it real quick if he knew that some trouble might result in it. They say that the Marines build men, but they have a strange way of doing it.

If I were you I'd try not to discuss anything about Bill and the trouble he has had with her. He isn't causing anyone any hardship now and the past should be forgotten, as far as that's concerned.

I sent Edna a postcard like the one I sent with your birthday card, which I hope you got in time. I wasn't quite sure of the date and wanted to make sure you got it in time.

Well, I'm getting pretty tired. I'll write a few more lines next week. So long.

Your son,

Mike

1967-10-12.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-10-12.text:
October 12, 1967
Bremerton, Washington

Dear Mother and Dad,

It has been about a week since I last wrote so I thought that I'd let you know how things have been going since then. I got your letter of Oct. 2 last Friday. Thanks for sending the clipping from the paper. It gave me some idea of what was happening back there. I meant to send it along to Bill when I wrote to him the other day but I forgot to. The next time I write to him I'll be sure to send it to him.

You said that you spoke to Brant's mother when they called about the records. Have they came by and got them yet. That guy is really in such a mess that he gives me every indication that he is a little crazy.

Tomorrow we pull out of this place and head for sunny San Diego. We will stop at Seal Beach, which is near Long Beach, and load ammunition all day Mon. We will go out the rest of the week and run some tests then get in San Diego Friday sometime. Unfortunately, I have duty that weekend and won't be able to see Bill if he gets liberty. I got a letter from him yesterday and he said that Sunday the 22th (thats the way he spelled it) he gets liberty on the base and that I could come out there and see him. If I can get someone to take my duty that day, I'll go out there. He said that he would have base liberty while he was up at Camp Pendelton so, it looks like we will be able to see each other while I'm down there.

I saw the final game of the world series on TV today. I am glad the Cardinals won it.

I've been on the ship for two weeks now. It seems like only a few days ago when I left on August 16th. I don't think that things could be much better than what they are here on the ship. The guys in the division are really good to work with and they think that I will have no trouble in getting acquainted with the operation of some of the equipment that we use. There are eight FT's and eight gunner's mates in the division. Of course, I work with the FT's.

I haven't had any opportunity to take many pictures with my camera up here. I will try to take some in San Diego and send them home.

I hope you didn't have any trouble putting that money in the bank that I sent home. Would it be just as easy for you to send some of those bank by mail envelopes and deposit slips to me and let me take care of it? If you do send it, send a book of checks also. Do whatever you think is best. As long as it is alright for you to put the money in the bank for me I don't see why I should have to bother with taking care of it from here. Just make sure that you keep the deposits recorded in the book, that's all hard-earned money. Speaking of money. Bill sent me $5.00 of the money that he owed me. That came as a surprise to me. He also said that he sent $10.00 home. Weather he sent it to Connie or you he didn't say.

It sounds like David is going to have plenty of hard work ahead of him in school this year. He better try to do the best he can if he doesn't want to take the year over. I am sure he will do better after he gets use to the idea that summer vacation is over with and its time to concentrate fully on his school work.

We had one of the generators go out yesterday and for a while every one thought that we would be staying up here for at least another week till it was repaired. They found out that the ship could get by without it and a new one will be put in at San Diego. I think every one will be glad to get away from here, especially me.

I wrote a letter to Georgia Mae last week and let her know that I would be back in San Diego this month and that I would like to come up and see them some weekend if it was okay. Actually, it was Sunday when I wrote to her and I haven't got an answer as of yet.

I have been doing a little looking into that 3rd class advancement. My leading petty officer went up to the ships office today and they called Treasure Island. They didn't have a thing about it, so the ships office is going to write a letter to the Reserve Center and see about it. I was talking to the chief the other day about it and I told him that after seeing what some of our duties would be that I felt if I had made 3rd class I may not be able to show that I knew what it was about. He said that he felt if a man passed the test that was all the proof he needed to know if a guy deserved the rating. He said that if it did go through and I didn't feel confident enough to take it that I could have it put off for a month or two until I had a chance to get acquainted with some of the dutys of the 3rd class. He said that he would reccomend me for the test in February if this deal didn't go through by then.

Well that's about it. There hasn't been too much to talk about this week. Perhaps the next time you hear from me will be if I call from San Diego next week. It's time to go eat supper so I had better go for now. Bye.

Your son,
Mike.

P.S.
You can start sending the Review now. Thanks.

1967-10-19.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-10-19.text:
October, 19 1967
San Diego, Calif.

Dear Mother and Dad,

At last, I'm back in San Diego. When I left here the first time I thought I was glad to get away from here but nothing could be any worse than up there in Washington. We got in about 4 o'clock this afternoon. We were not suppose to get in till tomorrow afternoon but things went off so well at sea that we got in a day early.

We didn't get any mail all week while we were at sea but they had mail call about 6 o'clock this evening. I was glad to get the card, your letter, the clippings and the Heath catalog. I really appreciated the card, it made me feel proud to be in here and glad to know that people on the out side are thinking about us.

I have enclosed a money order for $50.00. Please put it in the bank. Since you are not having any difficulty with the money, you can continue to handle my finances. Don't bother about sending the check book. I really intend to save a lot of money because there are a lot of things that I plan to do with it when this two years is over with.

It really stunned me to hear about what happened to David. I am glad he wasn't hurt seriously. Your editorial hit the nail on the head and I bet that woman had some trouble sleeping for a few nights if she read it.

I guess that deal with Allied will never come to an end. They haven't got a foot to stand on. Wasn't that stuff insured. Why don't they just forgetit then? I imagine grandpa is still hot on the idea of getting one of the county radios but he will have to forget about it now.

You asked me in one of your letters how I liked it when we went out to sea. I hoped you'd never ask. The first two weekends out I got seasick and the same thing happened last Saturday after we went out. But, I can assure you that I wasn't the only one who did. About 50% of the crew gets sick when we go out. The sea is really rough up there and that is the reason for it. I think I have overcame it and am used to it now. The sea was really nice when we started to get off the coast of California. We cruised at a condition III watch, (wartime crusing). This is really rough on a guy. The watches are four hours on and either four or eight off plus the regular daily work routine. I stood my watches in the gun director and believe me it is really cramped in there. There are three of us in there and it is like the inside of an Army tank. I lived through it and it wasn't all that bad come to think of it. We will cruise like this for the rest of the time before we head out on Jan. 16th.

That letter you got about the ship, you will get one each month. I put your name in and Bill's too to make him think how great our ship is.

I won't be able to get out to see Bill Sunday because it is almost impossible to get a standby this weekend. He will have liberty Monday and so will I so it looks like we can see each other after all. I told him how to call the ship if he wants to get hold of me and how to get out here if he wants to see me.

Tell Duce that I have some hats to send to him when I have the chance. They are a little frayed but should be okay for him. It sounds like he has been a busy boy with all the days off of school and his outside activities. I bet he really likes it when he goes over to Champaign. I would like to see him join the boy scouts, but if he is having a little difficulty with his school work perhaps it would not be such a good idea after all. I bet he is using my radio, just tell him to keep fresh batterys in it. ha ha.

After I write this letter I will only have two of the envelopes left. Send more if you wish to. I would like dad to send me about a dollars worth of mint commorative stamps similar to the ones on the envelopes. The postal clerk said that he noticed them on my letters and wanted to know if I had any with me. I expalined that my dad was a stamp collector and that he put them on the envelopes for me to send home. He is really a nice guy, he is rather old and has been in for over 16 years and I would like to do this as a favor to him. Send what you think is worth a dollar and he will pay me for them then I'll send you the money for them. I'll try to get him interested in a little more if I can.

Yes, it has been over two months since I left. Its hard to believe all the miles I'v traveled and all of the country that I've seen and I didn't have to pay a cent for it. Big deal! The time has really went fast and I have been on the ship for over three weeks.

I think I remember hearing about that guy that collects stamps and that is a little wierd, They ought to put their foot down and ban him from the stamp club meetings.

It was really something to see when we got in this afternoon. There were a lot of wives and realtives on the pier waiting for the ship to get in. The ship has been away from here for over three months and there were a lot of happy people when we got in. I can imagine what it will be like when we get back from the Wes Pac cruise.

Well it's about 9:30 now and I have to iron my dungarees before taps so I had better go. Write again.

Your son,
Mike

1967-10-24.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-10-24.text:
24 Oct. 1967
Tues.

Dear Mother + Dad,

I hope you get this before you send the clothes. Here is what I want, Levis permanent press pants both pairs (brown + blue), light colored permanent press shirt, pasley shirt, black belt (wide one), socks (green pair) and shoes.

I forgot to mention it, but I would appreciate it if you would send the '68 Allied and Lafayette catalogs. Also send any mail + have that you think I may be interested in.

Use this money for the postage.

I'm glad we had the chance to talk on the phone this evening. I'll write more later on in about a week. Bye.

Love, Mike

1967-10-31.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-10-31.text:
Oct 31, 1967
8:30 PM

Dear Mother and Dad,

I got your letter of the 23rd yesterday after we got back in port. It's really nice to have mail waiting for you after you've been out for a few days.

I hope you got my short note with the money before you sent the clothes. I got three of the newspapers today. It sure is nice to be able to read whats going on.

I sent the pictures to Bill and told him to send them back home when he finished with them.

Here is the first roll of film I took with my camera. You might wonder how Grant got that bad eye. I don't think I told you this, but I gave it to him. It took two stiches to close it up. I'll tell you some other time about it.

I guess the world is full of surprizes after what you told me about Jeanne. I wondered why they moved the wedding up from August to July, now its pretty apparent why. But from what you've told me it looks like they didn't move the date up quite enough.

I guess the one big thing on my mind now is weather to come home for Christmas or not. I'll have to talk to Bill and see what he is going to do then maybe make up my mind. I'm afraid that things may be just as boring as when I left and I don't want that.

I got the new envelopes and the stamps. I haven't had a chance to see the postal clerk but will probable sell them for face value.

It seems like just about every time you write, David is out of school. I bet he looks forward to the next day off so he can do what he wants to. Be sure to take a picture of him in his new suit. Tell him I said for him to keep those new shoes shined up.

So he out Halloweening tonight?

Out of the clear blue sky today I got a check for $17. This was to cover my eating and living expenses for the trip from San Diego to Seattle. Needless to say I again made money on that deal.

Do you remember that big box I left laying in the closet floor in the back bedroom? If you look in there you will find a question and answer book titled "Military Requirements PO 3 and 2". Send that out here as soon as you can. If it isn't there look every where you can. I think that Swinger camera and some other Navy papers were in there too. I need this because that damned reserve center did not enter it in my record that I completed the course. I have to do this over again real quick in case I have to take the test in Feb.

I will most likely go up to see Georgia Mae this weekend. I can leave here at 4 PM Friday and don't have to be back till Monday morning. I am going to try to get in touch with Bill and see if he can make it too.

I hope you will like your new job at Roosevelt. I imagine working the extra two hours won't be too hard to get use to.

Well I hope I didn't forget anything to say. I have one more letter to write then will get ready for bed. I'll write again. Bye

Your son,

Mike

1967-11-12.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-11-12.text:
Nov. 12, 1967
San Diego, Cal.

Dear Mother and Dad,

I got your letter along with the correspondence course last Thursday. I got the clothes the same day. It has been a while since I last wrote so I had better try to write a few lines now.

Last weekend, as you know I went up to Georgia Mae's. I got there about 7:30 Friday night. We had given up hope on Bill and were eating supper when he called. I was really glad to see him and I could tell he was glad to get away from there even though it was a short weekend since he didn't get there till about 6:00 Saturday evening. They were sorry that there was not enough time for them to take us anywhere but it was fine just to be able to relax and take it easy. We had plenty to talk about and it was a good weekend as far as I was concerned. Since I have duty on Thanksgiving day I will probably go back up there on the weekend after. I don't know just what Bill's liberty will be then. Sunday evening they took Bill back to Camp Pendelton then brought me on down to San Diego. I took them on the ship and showed them around after we got here.

We left port Monday morning and were suppose to be gone till Friday but we got back a day early on Thursday. This was good and it was planned to give us all day Friday off to commerate Veteran's Day. This didn't strike me to much because I had duty Friday. Well, before we even got in Thursday we were told that the plans had been changed and that we would most likely be going out again on Friday morning for some special operation. Then the news came out about the President coming out here and we were to be one of the ships in the task force with the Enterprise along with about five other ships. Saturday we got back in about 11:00.

Bill was waiting on the pier when we got in. I brought him on the ship and we ate dinner then went into San Diego and spent the rest of the weekend there. He left this afternoon about 2:30 for Pendelton because he had to be back at 5:00. We went out to the zoo and Balboa Park yesterday afternoon. It is really nice out there and quite a change from the downtown district.

I have got a locker for my civilian clothes and Bill is going to put his in with mine when he gets some. I havent wore mine yet but will when I get my next weekend liberty which is the weekend after Thanksgiving.

I hoped you watched the papers closely in regard to the President being here. It would be nice if our ship got mentioned but they probably gave all the publicity to the Enterprize.

I have some more pictures to send home that I took here on the ship and at Georgia Mae's. They should be ready about Thursday. Thank's for sending the picture of David. I haven't forgot what any of you look like but it does help me to remember the ones back home.

The other day as I was looking at one of the newspapers, I just happened to notice the rates for the subscriptions. From what I could tell it is $24 for the year. I think that is rather expensive. If you would, I would rather have you change it to Sunday only. Do what you want to but I wanted you to know what I thought about it. I do enjoy reading all the news even though it may be old news.

If I do make it home on leave, I'll go down to the reserve center and see what I can do about that advancement. If not, I'll just let things take there course and see what happens.

Something else I noticed in the paper. The police department is getting a new radio communications system. I wonder if this will effect our still being able to pick them up on the radios.

As you might notice, some of these stamps are in rather poor shape. When the package came one of the second-class petty officers in the division decided he would be a wise guy and peel them off for me. I let him know that the next time he pulled a stunt like that with any of my mail he would be sorry he did. I kept the ones that wern't too bad. I hope you can still use them. I doubt if it will happen again because I think he got the idea that I meant what I said.

I wonder what you are sending in the package you mentioned in the note. I imagine I'll be suprized and happy to get it.

I have got a course on fire control to help get me ready for the test in case I have to take it again in February. As soon as they get some applications, I am going to take out the courses on electronics. These count as much as three hours credit at junior college level. It costs $5 for the first one and the rest are free. You get to keep the textbooks that they furnish so this is a good deal.

We will be in port for 18 straight days before we go out again. We go out that time then will be here till the middle of January when we leave for West Pac. Bill said that it will be the monsoon season over there then so I imagine we will have some bad weather at sea for a while.

Bill got his liberty Friday at 3:00 so he spent Friday night here in town by himself. He got pulled off of the sidewalk by one of those photographers who take pictures then tell you to come back the next night and see the proofs. Last night we went back to look at them. I think the guy was a little dissapointed to see that Bill brought his older brother back with him. Get this, they wanted $5.25 for a 5x7 black and white. We didn't stay there long. I warned him to stay away from those joints because they are all out to take your money. They don't bother me but they can tell a guy who just got out of boot camp and figure they can take his money.

Tell David to keep up the work in school and before he knows it Christmas vacation will be here. It sounds like he has figured out some good ways to try to get sent home early.

Well, it's about time for the movie on the base to start so I had better close here. Let me here from you again when you have time to write. So long for now.

Your son,
Mike

1967-11-20.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-11-20.text:
Nov. 20, 1967
Monday

Dear Mother + Dad,

It's been about a week since I last wrote. I have got two letters from you since then, one of them came today.

I hope this letter brings you good news. If you noticed the return address, I am now third class. I found out last Wed. and sewed the "crow" on today. I figure I have about $123 in back pay coming. I'll get this next pay day. Now I'll get $84 a pay day instead of the usual $65. So, I should end up with about $200 pay next time.

It really feels great. Its like getting your report card and finding out you passed to the next grade. Now, I've got a chance to make second before I get out.

I have decided to come home for Christmas. I will be home for about 14 days starting on Dec. 19th. Of course, the way they run things here, there might be something to change that somewhat. But at any rate, it's a pretty sure thing.

I'm glad to hear that Bill's car is back. It should help boost his morale, if he makes it home.

This weekend I'll probably go up to Georgia Mae's again. She said she would like to have us up there for the Thanksgiving holidays, but I have duty Thanksgiving day and won't be able to make it till Friday evening.

I would have liked to talked to grandma that day when she called but of course I was asleep. I think it did more good for Bill to talk to her than it would have me.

We had our first rain here yesterday in over seven weeks. The weather is so nice I can't believe it. I will have to be ready for the cold weather when I come home, so had better get my p-coat cleaned.

I really can't think of what I would like for Christmas. There isn't anything I need and I wouldn't have any room to keep anything I could use. I'll give it a lot of hard thought and try to come up with something by the next time I write.

I hope you like these pictures. Bill sent the ones you took to Georgia Mae and she sent them on to me to send back with the ones I took.

I still haven't got that package you wrote the note about. Perhaps it will get here tomorrow or the day after.

I am glad to hear that one of the radios got there. I would rather have you let that man in Springfield put them together than wait for me to do it at Christmas. I intend to use that time for rest + relaxation and would rather not be occupied by that.

Danny Wiggins predicted to Bill and me last summer that someday he would be a family man. I guess he is getting off to a start. He ought to stay in the Army for another six years, they could really use his kind. ha ha

We have one more operation to go out on. This one starts next Monday and lasts for about 5 days. We'll be here in port till the 16 of January when we go on the operation that really counts.

It sounds like Daddy is keeping pretty busy around the house and with the stamp auctions. I suppose the new stove ought to make the food taste better, but come to think of it, it always was pretty good. Tell David not to get too lazy over the holidays and to keep at his school work. He can start to slack-off after the year is a little over half way through, but its the time now that counts. I'm sure he will get through this year in pretty good shape.

I'm glad to hear he is taking an interest in the glee club at school.

You might be wondering why I haven't sent any money home for a while. I have lent quite a bit to Bill and am saving most of it to come home on. I'll probably put some in the bank when I get home.

Its almost 7:30 here and I have to iron my dungarees for tomorrow then will go over to the show on the base. I'll be waiting to hear from you & again and will write in about a week.

Bye

Your son,

Mike

P.S. If you "happen" to see Bill before I do, give him these "portraits" of himself.

1967-12-05.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-12-05.text:
Dec. 5, 1967
Tuesday

Dear Mother + Dad,

Another week at sea and now we are back in port. I got the letter Dad wrote today. We got back here about 1500 today. We got as far north as 90 miles out of San Francisco. The next time we go to sea it will be for good.

It's really great having got this new rate. I got $207 payday of which $143 was back pay. Yes there are a few fringe benefits that I've waited a long time for. But they could never give me enough benefits to make me stay in here any longer than I have to.

Bill will probably be on his way back here tomorrow. I hope we can see one another before I come home.

I was surprized that you called me at Georgia Mae's that Friday. I figured you might call me there that weekend but wasn't sure.

That picture of Bill really makes him look happy. He looks like a real "Devil Dog."

You might know, the first day we get back, I have got duty. I have a four hour watch that starts at 2000 (8 PM).

I got reservations on American Airlines. Enclosed you will find my flight schedule. I think I'll call when I get in Chicago and let you know I'm on my way. I'll call after 4 PM from O'Hare airport.

It really seems strange that it's cold and snowing back home. The weather is really great out here.

Since you mentioned buying my return ticket that will be fine for Christmas. Actually that is what I had in mind if I were able to make it home.

I'm sorry this is so short but there hasn't been much happen during a week at sea. I'll let you hear from me once more before the 19th. Bye.

Your son,

Mike

1967-12-06.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1967-12-06.text:
Dec. 6, 1967
Wed. 9:15 PM

[Written on USO "A Home Away from Home" stationery]

Dear Mother & Dad,

I got the letter that mother wrote on the 28th, today. I kind of rushed the letter I wrote last night so will try to say a little more here.

I got early liberty today at noon. I went out to the airport about 3:30 to pick up my tickets. While I was on the way there I decided that I'd wait around for Bill and see if he came in. Sure enough, his plane got in at 4:20 and I met him there. He just caught the 9:00 bus back to Camp Pendleton a few minutes ago. From what you wrote and from what he told me, I guess he really had a high time. He is lucky he didn't get into serious trouble over that car wreck. He should be keeping out of trouble for a while now that he's back in the care of the USMC.

I didn't mention the money he owes me yet, but will if I see him this weekend. In case you're wondering how much it is it's $45. I have to give him a lot of credit though for going out and working those three days.

I'm starting to get things done and taken care of that have to be done before I go on leave. It seems as if there is always something you need to do or buy and have to run over to the exchange to take care of it. By this time next week, I should have just about everything ready to come home.

Bill has put his civilian clothes in the locker here with mine. He had to pay $2.50 for the rent and .15¢ for the key. We got out of our uniforms as soon as we got back from the airport and put on our civvies.

I bought him a wallet for his birthday and gave it to him today. He had been using an old one of mine that I let him have when I saw how ragged and beat-up his was. I figured this would be something he could use and would like.

Tell David that I'll try to gather up enough energy to take him hunting at least once. Maybe we can have some better luck.

Oh yes, I got your cookies and candy about 10 days ago. It was pretty shook up and crumbly. One of the guys in my division said that if you had put more popcorn in it it wouldn't have got so shook up. A couple of days later I got the candy from the Marine League. I shared both yours and theirs with the rest of the guys in the division. They thought it was pretty good and so did I.

Thats about all there is left to say for now. Its about time for this place to close so I had better get going. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-01-04.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-01-04.text:
Jan. 4, 1968
Thurs., 8 PM

Dear Mother & Dad,

As you know, I made it back out here okay, its really nice weather here but I still feel a little lazy after the two weeks leave. I guess I'll be back in the routine by the weekend.

Bill is going up to Georgia Mae's Friday night and I will get up there Sat. afternoon.

Its really going to be different when we leave here on the 16th. The liberty won't be often or as good but the time will go by pretty fast and before you know it we'll be back in the states.

We are having a lot of inspections this week and next. Next week we go up to Seal Beach and load ammo on Thursday and get back Friday. I wish I didn't have duty the last weekend here, but thats the way it goes.

Do you remember me telling you about that other 3rd class wanting me to take his duty? Well as I figured, he wanted me to take it for him Wed. I turned him down though, because I didn't feel like standing duty the day after I got back.

Tell David that we will get the boots next week and send them home when we have a chance.

I got the watch for Dad and got a band too. I hope he likes it. I also got grandpa a lighter. I'll try to mail them home this weekend from Georgia Mae's.

Heres my W-2 from the Navy for my active-duty. Put this check in the bank. We get paid again next week and I'll send home some more money.

Bill seems to be doing real fine. He too is getting a little itchy about leaving the states, just as I am.

I took the test for the Navy drivers license yesterday and passed it. I made a few mistakes but nothing bad. When my state license comes just send it on out here to me.

I am glad I did come home during the holidays. I think it helped my morale a lot and I'll be able to face the months overseas a little better.

I suppose David was really anxious to get back to school. Tell him to be good and work hard on his home-work.

Well, I have to go now and thats about all there is for now. I'll write again, soon.

Your son,

Mike

1968-01-14.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-01-14.text:
Jan. 14, 1968
Sunday

Dear Mother & Dad,

Even though I am going to call tomorrow night I thought I'd go ahead and write. I owe you a letter anyway.

Today is Sunday and things are pretty quiet around here. Its 73° outside now and a real nice day. I wish I didn't have duty this weekend but thats the way it goes.

I served mass this morning for the chaplian. He said I did real good.

I drove one of the guys into town to pick up the mail this morning.

I was suppose to meet Bill here Friday evening, but he never made it for some reason. Maybe he is on his way over now.

Georgia Mae called me here on the ship yesterday and wondered if I'd heard from him. She thought she would be up there this weekend if he could make it.

I played the tape recording for them. They liked it but those kids couldn't sit still or be quiet during the whole thing.

I'll send those Christmas pictures back but I have some I'm waiting for to send with them.

I saw the movie "Valley of the Dolls" the other day. Its really a good movie, see it if you have a chance.

Things have been pretty busy on the ship in the past week. We have had a lot of inspections and they have been loading stores about every day.

Tell David that the boots are on their way. We mailed them from Oceanside, Tuesday evening. (Jan. 9)

I have got my civilian clothes ready to go. I may take them up to Georgia Maes Monday if we get liberty early.

I hope you can get things straightened out at work. I am sure it will work out okay if you can get back to only four hours.

I don't like this job either but all I can do is bear with it. Thats one thing about Navy vs civilian life, if you don't like it you can do something about it but not in this outfit.

My electronics correspondence course was waiting for me when I got back from leave. I have done 2 of the 25 lessons. It is a good one and is easy.

I hope you get the package with the watch okay. Georgia Mae was suppose to mail it for me last week.

Well thats about it for now. So long, I'll write again.

Your son,

Mike

1968-01-21.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-01-21.text:
21 Jan., 1968
Sunday

Dear Mother & Dad,

Things have been going just fine since we left San Diego at 10:00 Tuesday. We are close to Pearl Harbor now and should get there about 4 PM today. We have some gun shoots to go through today then head for port. They have scheduled today as a payday so that liberty in Hawaii will be a little more enjoyable.

I got back to the ship about 5 PM last Tuesday. Bill called us at Georgia Mae's about 10 Monday evening. We had tried for about 30 minutes earlier in the evening to get a hold of him but didn't have any luck. We were glad that he called. I stopped at Oceanside on the way back to San Diego and saw him for an hour or so. That was a long night but since it was the last time I'd see anyone I knew, it was worth it.

The ship has been riding pretty well. The first day was hard to get use to after being in port for such a long time. I am use to it now and it doesn't bother me a bit. The first night a lot of us had trouble sleeping because of the rocking. I am eating pretty good so I guess thats a good indication I am in good health.

The days have been sunny and fair. You can notice it getting warmer the farther west we go.

We will be in Pearl Harbor for three days. It should be quite an experience the time we are there. Our next stop is Guam then on to the Phillipines.

One other ship left with us and we have been running side by side all the time. It gives you something to look at and at least we know we aren't the only ones out here.

I hope the weather isn't getting any worse back home, or could it get any worse? I'm sure David is having plenty of fun in the snow.

We have a calendar back here in the gun control room that we are keeping track of the days on. We figure the longest the cruise could last is 190 days (July 30). That seems like a long time but some day we will be able to look back on all the days as a lot of new experiences for most of us.

In my spare time, I've been keeping busy working on my electronics course. I have done three of the lessons since we left Tuesday. I stand my watches here on the radar console.

Thats about all there is for now. I'll write again when I know the mail will be going out. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-02-02.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-02.text:
Friday 2, Feb.
1968

Dear Mother & Dad,

How is everything back home? Its been over two weeks since we left San Diego and the days have really gone fast. Actually its hard to tell one day from the other out here. I hate to say this knowing how it is back there, but it gets quite warm during the day. They let us go around in T-shirts and that sun is really hot, just like summer.

I had a good time in Hawaii and hope we stop again on our way back. I have three rolls of film being processed now and will send them to you as soon as I get them.

Tomorrow morning we arrive in Guam. We will only be there for about 8 hours then are on our way to Subic Bay, Phillipines. That will take about 6 days. After that we go to Da Nang for a couple of days then off the coast of N. Viet Nam for about 40 days.

Have you heard anything about Bill? I suppose he is over there or on his way by now.

We have only got mail once since we left the states and that was in Pearl Harbor. There should be some tomorrow. After we get into the combat zone they will fly it to us about twice a week. That will be better than none at all like it has been.

Tuesday morning I began working topside where we have two of our directors. As you know I had been in the gun control room as a working space. They decided to switch me and this other guy around for a while. I like working out side in the sun and I find things pretty easy up there. I still stand my four hour watches on the radar console as before. I'm still keeping busy on my correspondence course and find it keeps some of the time occupied. Believe me there is plenty of that (time) out here.

The way things are shaping up over there, I hope we don't get extended while we are here. It would just be my luck that things would get real serious and they would extend the reserves about the time I get out.

By all means keep up the prayers for Bill and me, because there is no safe place when you are in the combat zone. We figure to draw combat pay 5 months of the 6 so you know we will see some action.

I hope David is making good use of the boots. I'm sure he is quite proud of them. How is he doing in school. Good, I hope.

Is there anything like cameras, radios, silverware etc., that I could get anyone while I'm over here? I have a few things that I am going to get.

I'm sorry but there isn't really too much to tell about. When you're out here not too much happens. But I do know for sure that there will be a lot to talk about the next time you see me.

I have to close here and will write again when I know the mail will go out. So long for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-02-04.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-04.text:
Sunday 4, Feb.,
1968

Dear Mother & Dad,

We left Guam yesterday at 1800. I was glad to get your letter and hear about the news back home.

We should arrive in Subic Bay around 1700 Wednesday, the 7th. I figured I'd go ahead and write now because mail will be going out there.

We had six hours liberty while we were in Guam. You remember my telling you about that buddy of mine from "A" school. Well, his ship is home-ported in Guam. His ship was in yesterday so I went over and saw him. He was glad I made it over and was pretty surprized. He said his wife had a baby girl on Dec. 7. He showed me some pictures and is pretty proud and would really like to get a couple of weeks leave but no chance of it. We had plenty to talk about and later on went over to the E.M. Club for a couple of beers. He was suppose to mail a letter, some postcards and pictures for me, you should have got them by now.

I was glad to get my pictures and the one of Bill. The one Uncle John took is at least something I can look at occasionally and think of you back home.

I'm glad David has been doing so good in his schoolwork. I bet he'd wear those boots to bed if you would let him.

Last week the captian was talking to the crew. One of the first things he said was, "No one is going to take the Jouett into port." We will be operating off of N. Viet Nam but from what this buddy told me there isn't really that much action at sea. He said it gets to the point where you don't even know there is a war.

I got a letter from Bill yesterday and he said he was to leave for Nam at 0930 on the 30th of Jan. I wonder if we will be fortunate to see one another over there. Only time will tell.

Since this is Sunday afternoon they have planned a jam session at 1430 for the entertainment of the crew. It will be a sort of talent show and will help take the edge off of the usual routine of the cruise.

I hope you liked the pictures. I have one more roll yet to get. I should get it in Subic Bay. If Dad can get some of those large envelopes (that I send the pictures in) at work, I would like some more. I only have one left and it may be hard to get some more.

Well thats all from this part of the world. Take care and keep me up on how things are going back home. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

P.S.

Can you figure out how far from home I'll be when we get in the Phillipines, Wednesday. By my figuring its about 8000 miles. Am I right? Let me know just for curiosity.

1968-02-08.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-08.text:
MIKE DUCY TO HOME — MANILA POSTCARD
February 8, 1968, from Subic Bay, Philippines
Postcard: "An Aerial View of Manila, PHILIPPINES"
2 scans (front and back)

========================================================================================
FRONT
========================================================================================

[Color aerial photograph of Manila, Philippines, showing the Pasig River
winding through the city center, the Intramuros walled district, Jones Bridge,
and surrounding urban area. Large neoclassical government building (Manila
Central Post Office) visible at river bend.]

Caption: "An Aerial View of Manila, PHILIPPINES"

Published by Kruger (#17501)
"Exclusively Distributed by National Book Store, Manila"


========================================================================================
BACK (Mike's handwriting, blue ink)
========================================================================================

8 FEB. 1968.

I GOT THE PACKAGE YESTERDAY, WHEN WE GOT HERE IN SUBIC BAY. I'M NOT SURE
HOW LONG WE WILL BE HERE BUT YOU CAN BE SURE IT WON'T BE FOR LONG. I HAVE
HEARD FROM BILL A COUPLE OF TIMES BUT NO ADDRESS. NO DOUBT ABOUT IT, HE IS
IN 'NAM BY NOW. I AM WAITING FOR MORE PICTURES AND WILL WRITE WHEN THEY COME.

                                        MIKE

Addressed to:
   MR. & MRS. DAN DUCY
   1525 N. ELLEN
   DECATUR, ILL. 62526
   U.S.A.

Stamp: 8-cent U.S. Air Mail (red, Capitol Building design)
Postmark: FEB 10 [year partially obscured]
Handwritten: "AIR MAIL" in blue ink with underlines


========================================================================================
NOTES
========================================================================================

First Subic Bay port call of the deployment, approximately February 7-8,
1968 (per logbook). Mike received a package from home upon arrival.

The most significant detail is Mike's mention of Bill: "I HAVE HEARD FROM
BILL A COUPLE OF TIMES BUT NO ADDRESS. NO DOUBT ABOUT IT, HE IS IN 'NAM
BY NOW." Bill (Pfc. William P. Ducy, USMC, 7th Communications Battalion)
arrived in Vietnam in February 1968 but had not yet sent Mike his mailing
address. Mike knows his brother is in the war zone but cannot write to him.

The brothers would eventually meet face-to-face in Da Nang Harbor on
June 13, 1968 — four months after this postcard was written.

The postcard was purchased at the National Book Store in Manila, a major
Philippine bookstore chain. Subic Bay Naval Station was located on the
western coast of Luzon, about 60 miles northwest of Manila.

This is the second postcard in the collection. The first (July 9, 1968,
from Guam) was sent on the homeward voyage.

1968-02-09.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-09.text:
9 Feb., 1968
Subic Bay, Phillipines

Dear Mother & Dad,

I know I just wrote to you a couple of days ago but, in the meantime I have received the package, your note with the W-2's, and a letter today, so I figure I have some writing to do.

When the tax refund comes, just put it in the bank. Take these money orders and do the same. I figure after the tax refund I'll have about $500. Am I right?

No one really knows for sure what ships we will join when we leave here. One thing is for sure, we'll be in the combat zone at last.

This is a pretty nice base here. There is a lot to do without going into the town. They try to discourage that because its not the best place to go on liberty. In case you wonder just where we are, its about 50 miles west of Manila.

This afternoon I took some of the guys from the division to pick up some machine-gun ammunition in the pick up truck. As is usual we didn't get it because of a lack of proper authorization on the part of the ship. At any rate it helped waste the afternoon. Tomorrow is Saturday and a full working day. They just don't let up, but I can say that I don't really exert myself too much.

Thanks for taking the time to have those extra pictures made. She will be glad to get them. The picture here was taken by one of the guys one afternoon while I was on watch.

The package arrived in good shape and got here on the 7th, the day we got in here. I was really glad you sent it. Thanks a lot.

Bill has wrote a couple of times but hasn't sent a new address. He wrote when he left the states and sent a card from Hawaii.

I am expecting some pictures back any day, and will send them when they come.

You and David might be counting the days till school is out, but you can be sure that I'm counting the days till we get back in the states. We are over three weeks out of the states and really a long way from home.

I have been doing pretty good on the course. I think I will put in for the test and take it before I finish the course, you can do this if you feel you know the material.

I think I'll have you cancel the newspaper subscription as soon as it runs out. I enjoy getting it but when you don't get mail every day the papers are pretty old by the time you get them. They print up papers off of the teletype when we are at sea, so you can see we aren't really shut off from civilization in that respect.

I'll probably go over to the E.M. club tonight and have a few beers then come on back to the ship.

That's about it for now. The next time you hear from me we should be off of 'Nam. Take care of everyone and write again.

Your son,

Mike

1968-02-18.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-18.text:
18 Feb., 1968
Tonkin Gulf,
Viet Nam

Dear Mother & Dad,

Today is Sunday and things are going pretty smooth. This afternoon we got mail for the first time since we left Subic Bay when the helicopter brought it aboard. I was hoping to hear from you and sure enough there was your card with the letter and pictures.

We left Subic on Tuesday, the 13th and in 48 hours were in Da Nang. We anchored in the harbor there Thursday and left Friday afternoon to go on station up here. Its been real cloudy and cool with a little rain ever since we got over here Tuesday. While we were anchored there I had an M-1 rifle and a clip of cartridges by my side during the day while I was topside working. When they say there are about 500 air strikes a day you better believe it. With all the air traffic a person might think he was at O'Hare or some other large airport. We could hear some shooting in the hills but we were in a safe place (I think).

I was hoping to get a letter from Bill today but nothing yet. I don't suppose he will have much time for writing.

I was glad to see the pictures. As I looked at them it made me feel like I was in a small way there with the rest of you. Even the snow outside looked good believe it or not!

I'm really glad you got rid of the car. All I can say is I have pity on the poor guy who bought it.

I'm happy to hear that David will be taking the drum lessons. He won't be sorry he did. By the time he gets in high school he should be pretty good and may get into a band. Then he could make a few dollars on the side and have a great time doing it.

The table in the picture was a nifty idea. It keeps the toys off the floor and all the better to sweep under, of course.

About my buying souveniers over here. On all the bases they sell the same things in the exchange that they sell in the city. The prices are cheaper and you know the merchandise is good. I would like to buy a stereo tape recorder if I can find the one I'm looking for. I'll bring something home for everyone as souveniers.

I have been keeping a day to day log of the days on the cruise. By the time we get back to the states I'll have a good summary of what and where we went.

By looking at the calendar I figure that there is only 18 more months left till August '69. I can't get over how fast these six months have gone. At times the days seem so boring and drag along. But when you look back on it, it wasn't so bad after all.

We will be here on station till around March 25 then go back to Subic Bay for a few days then up to Japan. The sea is real calm over here but we all realize that the waters are hostile as far as we are concerned. It is no longer just another operation off of California, this is what we have been waiting for. Everyone looks at this from a serious view and thats the way it should be. I often wonder about Bill, knowing he is close around here somewhere. I know he is going to have some hard times in the year he is over here and I also pray that he can make it okay. As for myself I can think of no better way and safer way to get in the combat duty and extra $65 a month than to be right here where I'm at.

Here are some more pictures to put in my album. I hope you have got the ones I mailed from Guam, the same day I mailed the letter, Feb. 4.

In one of your previous letters you asked if I have heard from Father Bauer yet. So, far I haven't but will let you know when I do.

Now that we have a helicopter on board we should get mail about every three days. So, keep writing because I'll get the letters someday. I hope this has brought you up to date on how things have been so far. No doubt, there will be more to tell the next time I write. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-02-21.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-21.text:
21 Feb. 1968
At sea, Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother & Dad,

Here's a few lines to let you know I got the envelopes and your letter of Feb 12 yesterday. I also got a letter from Bill. Of course he was very descriptive in his observations of the situation there.

No, as you probably have figured out by now Bill and I were unable to see each other in Da Nang. For obvious reasons that is not a liberty port and the only way I could see him would be for him to come out to the ship when he knew we were there.

I'm glad you gave me some indication of the mileage breakdown. I figure that Bill and I are about 10,000 miles from home now that we are here. It doesn't seem possible. Look on the map and find the Tonkin Gulf. We are in the southern part off of N. Viet Nam.

You mentioned baking bread. Thats a coincidence because they bake all the bread when we are at sea. Just like home!

I'm glad you have mailed the magazine to me. If it is Popular Electronics, they were suppose to have changed the address so it is mailed to me. Oh well just as long as I get it, I'll at least have something to read.

Tomorrow is payday. I will get $167. Thats tax-free base pay for two weeks and combat pay for 22 days. These are only a few of the benefits of being over here. Big deal, the pay is the main thing.

We should be getting mail brought out to us just about every day now. There is not much to look forward to out here but the mail makes up for some of the monotony.

Yes, I too was a little curious about the situation at the Greve's. I guess Larry is in for four years. Bill and I will have our time in and the rest of the guys we know will still have a long way to go. Have you heard anything about Mike Siebert. I read the article about the Bates kid in one of the papers I got in Subic. I kind of had him figured for that type. I guess he is afraid to let go of the apron strings.

Since I just wrote a couple of days ago there isn't much more news. I'll be awaiting to answer your letters. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-02-26.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-02-26.text:
26 Feb., 1968
at sea, Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother and Dad,

I got your letter of the 19th today. Although I just wrote a few days ago I am sure you are always eager to hear from me so I'll see if I can bring a few lines together. Any letters I get I usually like to answer the same day. The helicopter has been making a mail run every other day but starting today its suppose to be every day now.

I'm sorry to hear that everyone is down with the cold and flu. The weather is pretty nasty up here but I'm managing to stay in good health thanks to the great medical care of the Navy.

Good luck in getting into the nursing program. It may be the break you're waiting for.

I thought the clipping about the Cubs was interesting and found a little humor in it, considering the source. I'm sure going to miss sitting in front of the T.V. on weekends taking in the games, but someday I'll be able to enjoy the privileges of civilian life again.

Because of the weather being so bad up here there has been a limited number of air strikes in the north. As a result, we have just been cruising around waiting for something to happen. Over the weekend two planes did go down somewhere away from our station. They rescued the pilot from one with a helo from one of the carriers. The other ones they gave up for lost. There are three carriers operating in our vicinity. They are the Enterprise, Bon Homme Richard, and Ticonderoga. Watch for them in the news, of course they get all the publicity. The only time someone pays any attention to the other ships is when they get captured (the Pueblo).

This drawing is of a cabinet I would like to build for the stereo equipment I intend on buying over here. Maybe you might have some better ideas and I may think up a different style. But I like this one the best. Anyway, try to be on the lookout for some wood and hardware. Let me know what you think of the design.

Here are some more pictures. I probably won't have any more till after we get back from Japan.

They are trying to make plans to have a priest fly in on Sundays to hear confessions and say Mass. It will make things seem a little more like Sunday if it works out.

We observed Washington's birthday and had holiday routine. They had a bingo game, for the first time, and showed a movie in the afternoon besides the usual evening one. It was a good day and gave us a chance to relax a little.

Well, thats all the good (?) news from here. I'll be waiting for your letters and anxious to answer. So long for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-03-01.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-03-01.text:
Mar. 1, 1968
at sea, Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother & Dad,

Its Friday and just about 10 PM here. I am on watch now and thought I'd answer your letter of the 24th which I got this afternoon.

We refueled from an oiler tonight about 2000. It was pretty cold and windy up there but things went off okay. They sent some mail over to us and I got a paper from 11 Feb..

Yesterday a plane went down near us. In the afternoon we moved into the area but they only found the wreckage, no pilot. We have the remains of the plane and the helmet of the pilot on board. I took some pictures of it.

Twice this week we went to general quarters when they picked up MIG's on the radar, the closest they got was about 60 miles but we were manned and ready just in case. I suppose it was just an harassment because they stayed well out of our range.

You mentioned that Bill had said somthing about finishing up school. If he can't do it while he is in here, he can make use of the G.I. bill and get $130 a month to go to school on. I have been thinking a lot about this myself. I think I will go to a two-year technical school or a junior college and make use of the money. With what I have planned to save up, it should be no problem financially.

When you send the box I'd like some magazines to read. Newsweek, Look, Readers Digest, or Sports Illustrated is okay. They don't have to be new issues because I just want something to read and help pass some of the time. I could use a couple of jars of Fostex soap. They don't have any here on the ship and it works real good for me. Also how about a calender. I would like one about the size of a small wall calendar.

I would like to see Bill while I'm over here. It would probably boost our morale a little. Maybe the next time we are in Da Nang he might make it out to the ship somehow. I know we won't get liberty there, so its got to be up to him if he can make it.

Its been 19 continuous days at sea for us now. The 25th of March seems so far away when we go back to Subic Bay. There is very little to look forward to and when the mail comes it makes the day seem a little brighter. We haven't went on water hours yet which is a surprize to me. The food isn't too bad either but how can you compare it to anything else when thats all there is?

This seems to be David's best year in school so far. Maybe he is learning a little from the experience of his older brothers. Its good to hear that he is interested in his schoolwork and eager to get his homework done in school.

I suppose this is about all the news for now. I'll write again, bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-03-12.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-03-12.text:
12 March, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother + Dad,

I got your note with the crossword puzzles today and your letter of last Monday yesterday.

Everything is still the same over here. The weather hasn't changed a bit and the days continue to go by. We only have 11 more days on station then are to arrive in Japan on the 29th of this month.

Last Friday a chaplain came aboard and said Mass for the first time since we left the states. They are going to arrange it so he comes once every two weeks.

Yesterday an Air Force plane went down inland about 65 miles southwest of us. They made some attempts to find the pilots but gave them up for lost in a couple of hours.

I am having a years subscription of "All Hands" sent home to you. You might say its the Navy's answer to "The Leatherneck". It will give you some idea of what goes on in some of the operations and you just might read about the Jouett.

If I can find a tape recorder that plays cartridges, I'll buy one in Japan. Those type aren't in use too much yet and the only ones we have here on the ship are the ones like mine. It shouldn't cost much and it will be good to send messages back and forth. I'll be sure to keep an eye out for one.

I know I mentioned this before but would you let me know how much I have in the checking account. Also include the tax refund. I have been trying to keep track of it but would like to know the exact figures.

I read the newspaper clipping you sent me. That guy has a brother that is in the reserves also. At first I thought it was him but remembered he had an older brother.

Yes, if you can find some paper back books, I'd like for you to send them. Mysteries, science fiction or short stories are okay. I can do without any of the off-color type if you know what I mean. We usually trade back and forth with the guys and it helps to occupy your time if you have something to read while on watch or waiting in line.

I haven't heard from Bill lately but expect to any day. I suppose he finds it hard to write and may not have the time. I could write letters everyday but there would be nothing to write about. But as soon as I get one of your letters I am anxious to sit down and answer it.

I have sent the application in for the correspondence course test. I don't know when it will get here but in the meantime am going to cram up on things I need to know a little better.

We have had a couple of intelligence briefings since we have been out here on station. They point out on the map what operations have been taking place and how it involves us. Actually its a lot of the news that comes out in the "Stars & Stripes" but the explanation makes it more interesting. They say that at Khe Sahn there is most likely to be one of the most decisive battles take place soon. Of course the way news travels over here it may have been over by the time you get this letter. If you keep one eye on the map and another on the paper you will be pretty well informed about just what the score is over here.

What kind of bike is David planning on buying? How did he get the money, rob a bank? I think you ought to make him wait till school is out that way he has to be good till then. Only kidding of course. Tell him to be good in school and keep struggling along with the drum lessons no matter how hard they may seem at times. I noticed the little note he wrote on the letter and could picture him sitting down writing it.

I have held off long enough telling you, but I have grown a mustache. I started it on Jan. 28 and will probably shave it off in Japan. I don't really care for it but it is something a little different. I remember Bill telling me that he was going to grow a beard and the whole works when he got over here. They wouldn't let us grow beards so the guys had to settle on mustaches instead.

Well, thats all the "exciting" news for now. I'll be looking forward to hearing from you again and will keep everyone back there in my thoughts. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-03-16.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-03-16.text:
Mar. 16, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother + Dad,

Its a little after 7:30 PM Saturday evening. I got your letter of Mar. 1 and the calendar yesterday. Today I got a letter from Grandma that was postmarked Mar. 5 but I wrote to her yesterday so she should get it soon. The mail is very unpredictable at times. I guess its just like the weather.

I also recieved a letter from Bill yesterday which he wrote Feb. 28th. Figure that out if you can, they must send mail over here by carrier pidgeon.

You mentioned that Bouchey had malaria. That is something they worry about over here. Every Monday evening at supper they pass out these malaria pills for us to take. They make you feel a little sick the next day but thats better than being laid up in some hospital for a couple of months. I suppose those Marines welcome that because at least they can get away from here without having to take a bullet to do it.

Our next stop in Subic will be for such a short time I am sure I won't be able to look up that guy. We will probably anchor out in the morning and get underway early in the evening. Our only reason for going back there is to unload the helo and its crew and pick up some supplies and mail.

Only one more week left up here and in two weeks we will be in Japan. Everyone is looking forward to getting there and it should be good liberty providing the ship doesn't make us stay on board over the weekend like they did in Subic Bay.

If you can, would you send me some more information about that tape recorder you bought. The instruction book would be fine. I'd like to have some idea what its like. In case I have a chance to buy myself one I want it to match up with yours.

Today the ship had its 100th helicopter landing. Right now we have two on board. Ours is being repaired and in the hangar and a bigger one is on the flight deck.

About 1330 we had a fire break out in one of the radar power rooms. They got it put out quick and there was very little damage. It was an electrical fire caused by some overheated wiring. So today has been one of our more eventful days out here.

I think after I finish off this roll of film, I am going to start taking slides. No doubt I can buy a slide projector over here and they have certain advantages over prints.

I'm glad to hear David finally got to get his new bike. If he takes good care of it, it should last long enough so his next set of "wheels" will be a car (hint). With Easter vacation coming up I suppose he is getting eager and has a lot of things he wants to do then. I bet he talks Daddy into taking him to work at least one day. Its always good to hear that he is doing better in school, just keep at it and he will get along fine.

Its been 34 days at sea since we left Subic Bay. Everyone is in good spirits but I am sure we all could use a few beers right now. By the time we get in Japan I'm sure we all will be glad to set foot on land again.

That about sums it up for now. I'll try to write one more "free" letter while we are here, but if I don't you will hear from me in Japan. Keep the letters coming and I'll be looking forward to getting the package and magazines. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

P.S. Good luck on the diet!

1968-03-26.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-03-26.text:
March 26, 1968

Dear Mother + Dad,

By the time you get this letter I will be in Japan. We are on our way there now after stopping in Subic Bay for five hours Sunday. I got your card and the letter with the pictures then. As always I was glad to hear from you and its always nice to see pictures of those back home. David still looks the same and I can imagine the coaxing you had to go through to get him to pose for them. I am sending them to Bill and he will send them back to you.

The ship should arrive in Yokosuka about 1400 Thursday. You can't imagine how glad I'll be to get off this ship for liberty. After the 2½ months of this cruise I am well convinced this isn't the life for me. Some of the nonsense and fools you have to put up really get under your skin during these days at sea.

Since I have last wrote we have had two fires here on the ship. One was in a radar power room and yesterday a transformer burnt up. They were put out quickly and no one was hurt. Things like that can sink a ship just as well as anything else. But we have had everything go fine so far and no doubt it should continue to.

We left the Gulf of Tonkin Friday evening after 34 days up there. The chaplian came aboard and said mass that evening and we refueled from an oiler later in the night. That was one of the more active days up there.

I shaved off the mustache a week ago. I got tired of it and it was somewhat of a nuisance.

I had it figured right in regards to the amount I had in the bank. I hope to have at least twice that in there by the time I get back to the states.

Sunday I also got the package and the magazines. Thanks a lot. By reading the magazines I was reminded of some of the things that are going on in the world. There is only one thing we are concerned about over here and thats how the war is going so of course thats all you hear.

Thats all there is for now. I'll write from Japan. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-03-30.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-03-30.text:
Mar. 30, 1968
Yokosuka, Japan

Dear Mother + Dad,

I got a letter from you on Thursday the day we arrived and another one today. The package with the books and candy also came today. So it looks like mail is getting here real quick. I got one paper today dated Mar. 22, so you had better see if they have been cancelled.

Its Saturday evening here and I have duty today. It has rained most of the day and is rather cool outside. I had liberty the first two nights here and enjoyed a good steak dinner both times. Its a lot of fun to go out buying souveniers and jew down those peddlers.

I have sent some brochures on the stereo equipment I have bought. Save them for me. I have not got a turntable yet and may get one from Allied for a good price when I get back home. I can buy a cartridge recorder like yours for $34.00 and I'll get over to buy it next week. If you want to you can answer this with a tape and I'll send one back.

From what I have been able to pull out of the papers it looks like Decatur got beat out in the state tournament. Did they lose to Springfield? I have also noticed a lot of the guys Bill and I both knew have been either getting drafted or enlisting in the service. In a way it's nice to see someone else getting their share of time in this outfit. I would like for you to clip out the "Service News" sections of the review (Tuesday?) and send them to me.

Thanks for remembering to send the specifications on your tape recorder. I was almost sure what it was like but wanted to make sure before I got one.
