The Easter bunny in the box was really a surprize. We hung it up in our working space. I wonder how long it will be there before some one makes us take it down?

I have signed up for an all day tour of Tokoyo tomorrow. Providing there is enough seats on the bus I'm all set to go. In case you're wondering Tokoyo is about 40 miles North of here.

As for as a slide projector goes, I plan on buying one here. I think one of those slide viewers would be better for Bill and they should sell for around $2.50. I am going to get one here and I will be all set for slides. I also bought a pair of 16 x 50 binoculars here for $17.50. I have made all of my purchases here on the base at the exchange. You are guaranteed of good merchandise at the best of prices.

There is some rumor that we may make a final stop here before we head back to the states. If there is anything you need or want let me know ahead of time and I'll bring it back. I really don't think we will be here again but who knows. Its 2200 miles from Subic Bay and 4 days, one way so any extra miles of travel by then may be discouraged.

This month is coming to an end pretty fast. We will be approaching the half way point in the cruise in a couple of weeks. After those 45 days since our last liberty it was good to get off the ship Thursday and get some of that good American beer for 15¢.

I hope you have good luck in the L.P.N. test. How's the cafeteria union panning out?

Well I have to go for now and write a couple more letters. I'll be looking forward to a tape from you. So long.

Your son,

Mike

1968-04-19.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-04-19.text:
April 19, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother & Dad,

This morning I got your letter of April 12th. The mail helo is now coming in the morning so its good to start off the day with mail from home.

You should have got the tape by now that Bill and I made in Da Nang. We were glad to see one another and I was surprized he was able to make it. You know we have been pretty fortunate to see each other since we went into the service and I guess this is no exception even though we are over 12,000 miles from home.

Just one year ago I graduated from school at Great Lakes. The time has really went fast and it seems like only yesterday.

I can't imagine why Grandma & Grandpa weren't able to play the tape I sent them on their recorder. I don't remember what speed it was on but it should have been compatiable to be used on theirs. It was done on a mono recorder. Let me know what speeds they can use and I'll send the right speed next time.

I won't be able to mail you any recordings until you send me one. I used my last cartridge for the message from Bill to. So I hope to hear from you once again soon.

The routine up here hasn't changed a bit. The weather is still as bad as it use to be. But I do believe it has warmed up a little since our last time up here.

About the records Connie bought back. I think thats all there was. Bill didn't have a case of 45's and I think the ones he did have are with his stuff. From what Bill tells me she has started writing to him again now that the wedding is off.

I found the newspaper clippings interesting. I suppose it was quite a shock back there about Dr. King. The ships in the fleet flew the flag at half-mast for about five days.

On the first of May I will be working with the E.T.'s (electronic technicians) on maintence and troubleshooting. This is something I have always wanted to do and comes as a surprize to me. Actually we have more E.T.'s than we need even though two were discharged our last time in Subic Bay, so I guess it won't hurt anyone for me to be with them for the rest of the time over here.

I am waiting for one more box of slides before I send my slides on to you. I will make a tape to go with them so you'll know whats going on.

If you noticed any static like sound in the tape Bill and I sent it was some interference from one of the radars. Its pretty hard to find an ideal place to record here on the ship. But I think it didn't hurt the tape too much.

Well, thats about all for now. I hope you enjoyed our tape and found it interesting. So long for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-04-25.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-04-25.text:
April 25, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother, Dad and David,

I just finished a letter to grandma and thought I'd answer your letter of April 18 which I got today before I go to bed.

Things are still the same up here as they were before. The weather is a lot nicer though and we are getting some real sunny days instead of the fog and rain we were so use to.

Here is a clipping I thought might interest you. Actually this is about all I know about the recent move to slow down the bombing. Vinh is an airfield about 24 miles from us. We can usually see the explosions from the air raids there on a clear night.

I hope everyone had a chance to hear the tape from Bill and me and enjoyed it as much as we did in making it.

I am glad to hear you passed the LPN test and now can count on what you'll be doing next fall.

I got another box of slides today. As soon as I get another tape cartridge from you I'll send the slides with an explanation on tape.

I got two papers yesterday dated April 14 + 16. I am willing to read them if they are still willing to send them to me.

Here are some stamps I've saved for you.

The Stars + Stripes have pretty good coverage on the baseball season and it looks like the Cubs and White Sox are having a little trouble starting off on the right foot.

David, I got your note about recieving the souveniers I sent you. It was good to hear from you. You mentioned that you now have a pigeon and a duck. It sounds like you are going to start a zoo. Now all you need is some rabbits and a few more pets. On second thought a duck and a pigeon demand a lot of attention and they should keep you pretty busy. Keep at your schoolwork and be a good boy. Before you know it you'll be out of school for good and wish you were back in. So make the most of it now.

Well thats all there is to say for now. I'll be waiting to hear from you. So long.

Your son,

Mike

1968-05-02.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-02.text:
May 2, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother,

I got your letter of April 25 this morning after receiving your tape and the pictures yesterday. So I'll go ahead and answer your letter now while I have the time.

Yes, grandma devoted some of her last letter to me telling me how she noticed Connie was so lonely now that her wedding was called off. Big deal! The type of person that I know her as I'd say she brought her own "heartbreak" to herself. No doubt she'll find other interests soon enough and you most likely won't be seeing much of her then. Of course grandma never says anything to me about the past and if she ever does I'm telling you she is barking up the wrong tree. Its as simple as this; you were doing what you thought was right. Bill has managed to live through it and he should be growing wiser, the past is over and the best thing to do is forget it and chalk it up as experience.

This afternoon the chaplian came aboard and heard confessions and said Mass. I took time to attend both.

Our gun system is in pretty bad shape. The fire-control radar is down and we are waiting on parts. Two of the three gun mounts are down and also awaiting repair parts. It kind of makes a guy wonder just what we would do if we had to have some defense sometime. But we aren't out here alone and we know long ahead if we are in danger.

Just a short while ago two Migs were shot down by aircraft from the Ranger, one of the carriers out here. We sent our helo out to search for the VC pilots but I don't think they will have any luck. The action took place about 60 miles north of us.

As far as the correspondence course goes, I applied for the test at least six weeks ago and as of yet the test hasn't got here. I'll have to go to the office again and remind them of it. I want to get this course done and out of the way so I can start on another and this delay isn't helping a bit.

I'll be looking forward to getting the package and the books. Its rather hard to say how long it will take to get here but I'd say about two weeks at least, depending on how you send it.

Today the pay scale for the raise which goes into effect July 1 was posted. According to it I'll be getting $251 a month. Breaking that down that means I'll clear $50 a week. Really great! But thats more than I made in any job I had back home. I just hope I can save up as much as I am expecting to in the next 14½ months.

Well I'll close for now and get this in the mail. Bye for now.

Your son, Mike

1968-05-08.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-08.text:
May 8, 1968 12:30 am
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother and Dad,

I got your letter of April 29 two days ago on the 6th. I'm making an attempt to type this just to keep in practice so, over look any mistakes I may make.

Here are some clippings I got over here. I thought you may find them interesting to read. This afternoon we rescued two more pilots who were shot down about 1/2 mile off the coast. We launched the helo and in about 30 minutes they were back with the pilots. They were shook up a little but were not injured. We got with in 12 miles of the mainland which is the closest we have ever been up here. It was a real clear day and you could see a lot of the land over there. Things have picked up considerably since our last time up here as you can most likely tell in the newspapers. So, this makes four rescues for us and all of them in this line period.

We are suppose to rendevous with an oiler tomorrow night and recieve 1,000 pounds of mail which will be mostly 3rd and 4th class. There is a chance your package may be there, I hope so.

I haven't yet made any firm decisions on when I'll be taking leave. The first half of August I will be taking the test for second class so that means I will have to be here for that and any leave upon arrival in the states is out of the question for that reason. As far as your coming out here I don't think it is really necessary right now. I think it would be better to wait till Bill got back from overseas, then you could see both of us out here. I don't really know when I will be home next. It may be in the fall or after the first of next year. As far as Christmas goes I can't say. I don't really care for that travelling this distance during those holidays after my experience with making connections last time. At any rate it is a lot easier and cheaper for me to come home than for you to travel out here. So, for right now lets hold off and see when I'll be making my way back home. No doubt both of us will stay here on the west coast for the rest of our time and there will be plenty of time to make it out here later on.

I got word that I will be taking the test for the correspondence course tomorrow morning. Would you believe I applied for it on Feb. 27 and it just got here? I was told that one test for another guy took seven months to get here. It is believed that the test officer failed to mail the application out promptly and this may have been the case in regards to mine. I'll let you know when I get the drastic results!

We will be in Hong Kong in less than two weeks. They have been giving us a lot of stuff about keeping out of trouble there because of the Communist groups there. We'll only be there for five days then on to Subic for about three days and back up here. I am pretty sure I am going to buy one of those super 8 movie cameras in Hong Kong. I would like to take some movies over here and I know you would enjoy seeing them.

I sent off the roll of film with the pictures of Bill and me in Da Nang today. They are slides and I'll mail them to you when I get them back with three other boxes of slides I have taken over here.

I guess that's all the interesting news from over here. So long for now, I'll write again, soon.

Your son,

Mike

1968-05-12.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-12.text:
May 12, 1968

[Homemade Mother's Day card. Front has hand-drawn flowers (yellow, pink, blue) with hand-lettered text reading "HAPPY MOTHER'S DAY". Inside has the poem typewritten with hand-drawn flowers showing through from the front.]

Mother,

ON THIS SPECIAL DAY,
HERE ARE A FEW LINES TO SAY,
THAT TO ME YOU MEAN THE MOST
SO TO YOU I OFFER THIS TOAST
THAT IN THE YEARS TO COME,
TO ME YOU'LL ALWAYS BE NUMBER ONE.

Love,

Mike

[Handwritten note at bottom left]: Sorry, I couldn't get a card, so I had to use my imagination.

1968-05-13.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-13.text:
May 13, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother & Dad,

It's Monday evening here and about 7:45. Yesterday I got your letter, just one week to the day after you wrote it. I was glad to see the clipping of Bill and me.

Last night I got your package. We refueled from an oiler and they sent over third and fourth class mail. The Newsweek magazines were interesting reading for us. I guess the rioting in the big cities was really something. The paperbacks should be good reading during some of the hours up here. As for the pens, I can always use them. Thanks for everything.

I got a letter from Bill two days ago which he wrote on April 24. How about that service, 17 days to get here. He described an attack they had there and maybe this was the one you read about in the paper.

There was a destroyer hit up here by gun fire off the mainland. They were south of us and one day last week came up to our area. It wasn't too much and only one guy was injured. Maybe you saw it in the paper too. But that is what happens when they start cruising in too close to the beach.

The other day I got 20 newspapers. I read every one of them believe it or not. Three also came last night, the latest dated April 19.

I bet you are glad that school is almost over with all the trouble they have been giving you. And I thought things like that could only happen to a person in the Navy. I guess civilian life has a few bad breaks too.

Tell David to be expecting a letter from me in a day or so. I'll see if I can talk him into reforming a little.

Yesterday was a nice day and gave us a chance to do some sunbathing during holiday routine. I don't spend much time topside so its necessary to go out and get a little sun on your own.

I am really glad you are enjoying and using the tape we made. Don't wear it out though, because we didn't have a chance to play it back. I hope we didn't slip up on anything when we made it. Everytime you mention it I am so glad we took time to make it.

We got parts in for our radar this afternoon and I helped put them in. Right now we are letting it warm up and will be trying it out in a few minutes.

I hoped I would have got another tape from you by now. You said you would send a blank one in the package but must have forgot. At any rate I'll pick up some cartridges in Hong Kong and send a tape from there.

We have been getting quick news releases on the baseball scores. It looks like the Cardinals are hot again this year, the Cubs aren't too bad either but I wish they could at least play .500 ball. Its early in the season and a lot can happen to change the standings. I hope I can take in a few games at L.A. and would like to spend a weekend in San Francisco when I get back.

Well I had better close here. So long for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-05-16.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-16.text:
16 May, 1968

Dear Mother

Heres $200 more to put in my account. This should bring it to just shy of $700.

I am glad you did take time to say what you did on the tape. No, you didn't make me mad. I expected you would have some reaction and I was glad you told me. If you didn't it would have probably meant you had other ideas.

Well thats all I have to say and I hope you enjoy the tape as much as I enjoyed yours.

Bye for now.

Your son

Mike

1968-05-28.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-28.text:
May 28, 1968
Subic Bay, P.I.
Tues. 1900

Dear Mother + Dad, and David,

Here's a short note to let you know I received your May 23 letter today. I found all of the paper clippings interesting and good reading. I am glad everyone enjoyed the slides and tape. You should have got another set by this time.

We left Hong Kong Sunday and arrived here in Subic Bay Monday evening about 1700. I am staying aboard tonight and thought I'd stay sober for once. Only kidding of course.

Tell David I will mail his radio tomorrow or the next day. I don't know how well it will work to pull in the stations he wants to hear but I am sure it will be okay. Let me know how it works.

Thursday afternoon, Memorial Day, we have early liberty. There is suppose to be a Weapons department party for us. I also plan to see about your radio and go into town and take some movies.

We are moored alongside a tender which is anchored here in the bay. In order to go ashore you have to take a boat. This is a little inconvenient and not as good as being tied up to a pier. We are to leave Friday and head back to the Gulf for our usual operations.

David, I was really impressed by the picture you drew. You pictured it just right and have a good imagination. I have some coins to send you and will mail them in a few days. I think you are wise to hold off in going to camp this year. Wait till you make second or first-class then you can have more fun there.

I got a tape from Bill yesterday. His letters never say much but he sure had a lot to talk about on the tape. I'll send him one back tonight.

I hope I haven't discouraged your vacation plans any. Do what you want to, and I'm sure we all will be happy.

Mother, I'm glad to hear you got things straightened out with the school job. Things usually to turn out okay in the long run if you give them time.

Here are some stamps for Dad. I hope he has a place for them.

Well I must go for now. I'll be looking forward to getting your tape. So long.

Your son,

Mike

1968-05-31.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-05-31.text:
May 31, 1968
Subic Bay

Dear Mother,

Here is $100 more to put in the bank for me.

Yesterday was Memorial Day here and really a hot one. I suppose that you had the usual get together back there. Margaret Whiting was at the club last night and performed for about an hour.

I would like for you to send me two more jars of Fostex and a couple of bottles of M.F.C. I don't really need it but its good for preventive purposes and you can't find it over here.

We will leave here this evening and proceed on our usual route back on station. We are due for a short stop in Da Nang.

Well I have to go and get this in the mail. See you later.

Your son,

Mike

1968-06-13.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-06-13.text:
Thursday 9 PM
13 June, 1968

Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother and Dad,

Our past three days up here have been quite active with more than the usual everyday happenings. It all started about 3 AM Tuesday when one of our planes was shot down overland. The search continued into the next morning and one of the helicopters got hit by some small arms fire from some VC troops on the side of a hill. They landed back here and one of it's crew was hit in both legs from the machine gun fire. They gave him some treatment here then sent him off to the carrier for futher aid. They finally gave up the pilot for lost and called off the search. Later in the day one of the helo's on deck couldn't be launched because of engine trouble. We then proceeded to an aircraft carrier to have it lifted off by crane. Well it got dark by the time we got there and it looked like too risky of an operation anyway so they called that off too. Yesterday we set course for Da Nang to have another helo lift it off our deck. We got there about midnight and stayed over night. At 8:00 this morning they brought out a flying crane and lifted it off. We then got underway and are now back here on SAR station. They had some Migs get in pretty close up here this afternoon while we were gone but there hasn't been anything happen yet.

I got your letter of the 4th, today on Tuesday the 11th. As you can tell thats rather slow. We didn't get mail for three days and thats probably why. I decided to wait till today so I could mail these money orders. Today was pay day. Put $130 in the bank and use the $10 for the stuff I had you get me and the postage to mail it. Since you have already sent the box there is a good chance I may get it during our next refueling from an oiler which may be tomorrow because of the trip to Da Nang. We cruised at 29 knots (49 mph) all the way there and back. The only time we do get packages out here is when we refuel from the oilers.

I suppose you have got the tape I sent a few days ago. I hope every one liked it.

Have you started getting the "All Hands" magazines yet? I forgot to ask you many times. I suppose you have though, because I mailed in the supscription about two months ago.

I'm glad to hear David got his cast off and can go swimming now. How's he doing in summer school?

Well thats about all there is from here. I'll be waiting to hear from you again. Bye for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-06-29.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-06-29.text:
29 June, 1968
Tonkin Gulf

Dear Mother & Dad,

It's about 12:30 AM Saturday morning here and I'm on watch. I received your letter of the 21st day before yesterday on Thursday.

I got my two new courses in the mail the same day and have done three lessons on one already.

Yesterday was pay day. I drew $180 and will probably send some home after we stop in Subic Bay as I want to buy a few last items before we head home.

We get relieved up here at 8:00 AM Sunday then head for Subic Bay. We'll probably arrive there late Monday night and leave again Tuesday afternoon. Then it's a four day trip to Guam where we stop for fuel and mail. As I mentioned before, we cross the equator on the 10th.

Since I made the last tape on the 23rd, there hasn't been anything new happen up here. We had our last refueling here Wednesday night. Of course every day they have MIG tracking alerts several times but they seldom get within 40 miles from us.

We did a little bit of painting the past few days in order to have some of our topside areas looking good for arrival in San Diego. We'll finish up the rest of it next week. It's pretty hot outside during the daytime and that sun just doesn't let up. So as a result we have been taking our time and not doing too much at one time.

I just remembered this will be the last "free" letter I write from over here. Boy, thats too bad! We are starting to lose out on some of the combat zone benefits now that it's time to leave. But we will get the month of July tax free pay and they are talking about combat pay for that month too. But they aren't too sure and may have to deduct it from our regular pay later on if they aren't right.

I hope David is having a good time at scout camp. I'm sure he is enjoying it and it will be a good experience for him.

I'm glad you liked the dress material and have it made already. I'll be eager to see the pictures you took of it.

Well I'm sorry that this is so short but there isn't much more to tell. I'll be looking to hear from you when we stop in Guam. So long for now.

Your son,

Mike

1968-07-23.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-07-23.text:
Tues. July 23, 1968
San Diego

Hi Dad,

Its about 8:45 PM here and I am sitting in my rack writing this so I hope the writing isn't too bad.

I have duty today so that explains why I'm aboard now.

I had Saturday, Sunday and Monday off and of course went up to visit Mother and everyone else. I got back here on the ship about 3:45 this morning so that made it a long night for me.

Again I can't get over how much David has grown in the past 7 months. I set up my stereo equipment while there and he was really crazy about it. He thought that was just the thing.

We packed my things in their car to see if they would not take up too much room. The way it looks now they are going to be able to bring all of my things back with them. Mother and David are also carrying a few small items back too.

We recieved your letter that contained Bill's letter and pictures yesterday afternoon, so that gave us all a chance to read it.

If things go right I plan to leave here tomorrow morning and return Saturday at 7 AM in order to pay another visit up there before mother leaves as she is planning to on Saturday. If this doesn't work out I will go up Friday and tell them goodby.

I got a letter from Bill this afternoon. He sounds envious of me being back here in the states but sure wants another tour of that mess duty. As long as he likes it that's all that counts.

I ordered a turntable from Allied yesterday and it should arrive by express in a week or so if all goes well.

I also bought a movie projector while I was up there for the weekend. It works real good and everyone liked the movies I showed.

I hope things are going smoothly for you back there. Have a good time on the trip to Canada.

I have to close here so will see you later. So long.

Your son,

Mike

1968-08-23.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-08-23.text:
August 23, 1968
Friday 9:00 PM

Dear Mother & Dad,
     Here are a few lines to let you know I got your August 18 letter Wednesday and the letter of the 21st today. No doubt you have got my tape by now.
     I stood duty for a guy yesterday and charged him $7.50 for it. I am standing duty today for another guy but this one is free. And tomorrow I have duty myself. So I am spending three days in a row aboard without liberty. Sunday I plan on going into town and go to Mass then out to eat. In the afternoon I am going to a show then wash out some new pants at the laundromat.
     We have a two-day operating schedule next week that will conclude Thursday then its 7 straight weeks in port 'till our next exercise in the second or third week of October.
     Did you have any trouble operating the slide projector? How does the radio pick up Chicago stations?
     I didn't buy groceries at the exchange the last time I was at G.M.'s. She said she had enough food but sent me and John out a couple of times for groceries. I am willing to help them out but since she has advertized the fact around the neighborhood I am not going to offer to do it again. She should know better. When I saw the top of the sales slip on the page of the letter I didn't know what you put it there for but I see now. That saying makes a lot of sense. Anyway I think they are too lazy to drive over there to get groceries.
     I have an appointment at the clinic on the base for next Wednesday to have my foot looked at and worked on. I guess you don't have to raise hell with them just keep coming to sick call until they wise up and realize they can't do much for you. I must admit though that it feels a lot better and doesn't hurt to walk on so much. But it has to come off before it has a chance to cause too much trouble (if it already hasn't).
     Well its time to get a shower and hit the rack. I have the 4-8 watch in the morning. I'll write again next week. Bye for now.

                    Your son,
                         Mike

1968-09-03.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-03.text:
Sept 3, 1968
Tuesday 4 PM

Dear Mother, Dad and David,
     I got your tape last Thursday and your letter Saturday. I was going to write over the weekend but kept putting it off. Now I am at the library here in San Diego and have been doing some studying on my course.
     Yesterday was of course a holiday for us too. I slept till about 1:00 PM then went over on the base and saw a movie. While there I ran into one of the guys who was in my class at Great Lakes. We talked for a while then he took me around his ship and showed me what it
was like. The ship is a troop transport and they carry around 1200 marines at one time when they are operating overseas.
     I plan on going up to G.M.'s this weekend for the usual visit. I am going to call her tomorrow night and see if it is alright and let them know I'll be there.
     I was glad that you decided to keep the projector with you. Anyway I don't believe we are going to be receiving that many slides from Bill and I can still see them with my slide viewer. How
they see them is their concern. I would hate to have had them bring it back out here then we wouldn't be getting any slides to see; which may be the case. So again I say "Good thinking."
     I listened to what you had to say about the savings account and in some ways I'm not too sure about it. As of yet I haven't got any information about it from the bank. I feel that I will need that money a year from now and maybe it would be useless to put it in a savings account. I just
feel that it could be earning me a few dollars in the meantime instead of just sitting there. One thing for sure is it won't rot away, at least for sometime.
     I thought that last Wednesday I was to have my foot taken care of. Well, I got the days mixed up and am due to go over on the base tomorrow morning to have them look at it. But, it doesn't hurt at all now so I don't know what they will do.
     I too was a little startled at the ordeal you told of about grandpa
and the camera. I thinks the whole trouble was that he may have had some old film and that was why the pictures wouldn't come out.
     I got a new set of frames last week. I had to get them here in town because they don't have any optical shops at any of the base exchanges around here. They are similar to my old ones and are guaranteed for one year against breakage. I paid $18 for them which I thought was a little high but I doubt if I could have saved much more
anywhere else the way the prices are on things out here.
     Our weather out here has been so nice I can hardly believe that it has been so hot at times back there. Right now its about 75° outside and real sunny.
     I can see dad's reasoning on buying the groceries at the exchange commissary. It does make sense to me but I am going to ask about it before I go up there this week. But like I said before, I don't think they are too eager to go over there and
take the time to get the stuff. Perhaps she feels she is taking advantage of my coming up there and may feel this isn't fair to me. She didn't seem too energetic about it last time I was there but if she mentions it again, I'll get the stuff providing its okay. Actually I think we are worrying about something that isn't really as bad as it seems.
     I am glad to hear that David conformed to the punishment that he had no doubt deserved. I do hope he can have a better year in school and finds it a little
easier to do the work. I guess I can say the same for you too, mother!
     We still have been getting early liberty on the ship every day. But the duty days we usually have two watches and it gets a little boring but its only one out of every four days so I guess its not too bad.
     They are installing some new electronic equipment in the gun plotting room where I work. It is an addition to our radar that should improve its performance somewhat. It should take about 5 more weeks before we can
use it and test it out.
     Be sure to let me know if you have any difficulties using the stereo equipment or in hooking it up. Again I'll ask, how does it recieve the Chicago radio stations? I just wonder about how sensitive it is with the antenna it has built in.
     I suppose I'll head back to the base early tonight. There is a good movie there tonight and I'd like to see it. I have seen most of the ones playing here in town and occasionally they have some good movies out there.
     Well I guess this letter is running rather long. I had better sign off before you get a postage due on it.
     I'll write again or make a tape in a week or so. See you later.

                    Your son,
                         Mike

1968-09-18.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-18.text:
Wednesday 18 Sept. '68
7:00 PM

Dear Mother, Dad, and David,

     Even though I just called last night I thought I'd write to answer your letter I received Monday. I could have talked on and on about all that I was going to do when I got out and how thrilled and surprized I was but you know how I feel about it. It seems like I get the good breaks without any trouble. So you see God must be watching over me. I certainly hope and pray that this holds up and that come November I can get this Navy off my back with the exception of the weekly drills.
     I was very pleased to hear that things are going smoother for Mother at the school. How is David doing so far?
     I called Georgia Mae night
after I talked with you. She was really surprized over it. I told her I might take a few of my 17 days leave and spend some time with them. But of course I explained this may not be possible due to our personell shortage here. I told her I would see them on the 4th, 5th, and 6th of October. She brought Johnny home from the hospital the Tuesday after he went in. He had acid in his stomach was the diagnosis she gave me.
     Of course I am now faced with the pleasant task of getting all of my belongings together and shipping them home. I have two small tape recorders, my movie projector and camera, and a lot of civilian clothes to get back there. I will wait until the first week of October
to get things ready.
     Due to this coming up here are a few things I no longer have to worry about;
     1. extending my active duty if I make second-class
     2. when to take leave
     3. getting transferred to another ship so I can make another cruise again.
Some of the shock of this matter is starting to wear off but I won't believe it until I step off that plane in Decatur during the month of November.
     I mentioned a little about my past weekend on the phone. I had duty Friday and that was a real ------. I got called on the carpet because some GM left some magazines open. But I had a good defense and a first-class FT who stood be-hind me. The words were
really flying and I don't think I have ever been so mad at anyone since I have been in here. Along this same line the GM's left a magazine open Monday night with the key still in the lock and it really hit the fan then. But the FT's have been cleared for all of this and the GM's don't get liberty until 1800 instead of the usual 1530.
     Saturday this FTG3 who works with me and is married picked me up when I got off duty and we went over to his place to put in a rear-seat speaker in his car and some gauges in the dash. We got all of our tools from the ship. The speaker went pretty smooth, but the gauges were a little rough. I took my movies and projector over and we watched them
Saturday night. I stayed overnight at their invitation. They are also Catholics so we went to church Sunday morning. That was a real experiance because the Mass was a folk mass. Do they have these back home? We finished up the gauges later in the day and it looks like a factory installed job now. They are both my age and seem to be pretty happy and pleasant people for being married, but I guess its because they have no kids running around the house to cause confusion and trouble.
     I am going to buy a lot of clothes here at the exchange and send home before November. I can save a few dollars this way. I would also like to get a 12 gauge shotgun out here. They have some nice
ones like Bills for $88.
     Well I had better go for now if I intend on going to the base movie. See you later. Bye.

                    Your son,

                         Mike

P.S.
     I will send the pictures back later.

1968-09-24.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-24.text:
Sept. 24, 1968
Tuesday

Dear Mother and Dad,
     Today I received the letter you wrote Saturday. I also have the one you wrote last Tuesday here to answer.
     So far nothing new has came up in the past week since I talked with you on the phone. As of yet I still don't know the magic day in November but have heard two different stories. One is that they will keep us 'till the last day of the month and the other is that you get separated on your usual discharge date which makes it on the 15th of the month.
     I am glad you were concerned about mentioning the car situation in the last letter. You are right it is not the kind of car I was looking for. So you can see that my answer is one of "not interested." I gave the situation a
lot of thought before and especially this past week. Of course to have a new car would be my wish but I realize that this is a little out of the question because it would be necessary to have a steady job and be well established before undertaking such a venture. How soon, after I get home, I will need the transportation of a car or will be able to afford it of course depends on the fact of getting a job. But I do think I will settle on a late model used Chevrolet or Pontiac.
     Sunday I ran into a guy who was in my class at Great Lakes. We went to Tijuana that afternoon and got back about 11 PM. That place is really something. It reminded me a lot of some of the overseas ports but most of the places are cleaner.
There were a lot of tourists and sightseers there. It is easy to get yourself in trouble down there but we managed to come back alive and healthy. I suppose I will go down one more time before I get out and buy some souviniers.
     The past two days have been somewhat of a heat-wave out here. It has been very warm and sunny the whole day instead of late morning and part of the afternoon as usual. We are due to shift into blues the middle of next month so I hope the weather is accomodating.
     Friday night I went out to the stadium and saw the U.S.D. Aztecs play Northern Illinois University in a football game there. The Aztecs won 40-13 and about 35,000 were there. Northern looked pretty bad but the Aztecs are
the number one team in their college bracket. This guy on the Aztecs made a 67 yard touchdown run and that really brought the crowd to its feet and was worth my admission price of $1.00 (military ½ price discount).
     Well I had better close here and get cleaned up so I can go to the base movie at 8:30. I'll be looking forward to hearing from you again and counting the days too. So long.

                    Your son,

                         Mike

1968-09-27.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-09-27.text:
27 Sept. '68
San Diego

Dear Mother, Dad and David,
     Today I received a note letter from Bill on the 16th. Here are the pictures he finally sent. One funny thing is that he only used one 10¢ stamp and it wasn't cancelled. Also here are the pictures you sent me.
     Well, yesterday I celebrated my first year aboard the Jouett. Needless to say a lot has happened since a year ago and
much of it has been unanticipated.
     I am standing duty Saturday for this buddy of mine and Sunday is my day of duty. So I'll be spending my weekend on the ship.
     I am hoping to go to G.M.'s next weekend but may not make it because there is word out about having to
be aboard Saturday for an inspection of weapons handling proceldure. So I am not sure yet what my plans are.
     Well I had better close here.
     Bill said he is still on mess duty and is expecting R+R in October. His hut was blown over by a typhone (his spelling) and now he is living in a better one.
     Bye for now.

                    your son, Mike

1968-10-20.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-10-20.text:
Sunday, Oct. 20, 1968
7:00 PM

Dear Mother, Dad, and David,

     I just got done eating supper and am at the USO now to relax for a few moments and write a few lines. I've been up since 3:20 this morning and am begining to feel the effect. I stood the 4-8 watch aboard the ship and came into town about 9:00 this morning.
     I got out to the stadium about 11:45 AM today for the Chargers game. It started at 1 PM out here and may have been televised back home because I
saw the NBC cameras there. The Chargers beat the Denver Broncos and I believe the score was 55-17. It was a good game and their only home game this month. They had about 40,000 there and the weather was great for it. A Navy band and a drum and bugle corps from the boot camp provided the halftime entertainment. The reason for this was because today starts Navy Week with the Navy birthday next Sunday.
     After the game I came back downtown and went to 5:15 mass. There were quite a few people there too.
     When I finish this I plan on going out to do my laundry then head back to the ship.
     We get underway tomorrow at 0800 for 5 more days of operations then are back in port for a few more weeks. Last weeks exercises were the usual with a lot of confusion and too many mistakes. But that is why we are going out, so we can train
the new people and make the ship ready for another cruise. Sorry to say, but I don't plan on making that trip again.
     Monday morning the captain announced the results of the advancement exams. My name was among the others and I get second-class on December 16th. As a matter of fact I was the only person in gunnery division to pass the test. I was a little surprized that I made it and am glad I did.
     I hope you got the
three boxes I sent home. Last Saturday the express office was closed that day and I had to send them by Greyhound because I wouldn't be able to do it during the week.
     The same day I spent around $120 on things I got at the exchange at the MCRD. I got two sport coats and a new electric razor among them.
     You can expect me to send almost all the rest of my things home around the 9th of November.
     I am sure I'll be up to Georgia Mae's on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of next month. From what information (rumors) I have been able to pick up I may get discharged around the 16th, but I'm sure it won't be much earlier especially not during the first three days of the month. I am sending the pictures on to her tonight with instructions to return them to you.
     I guess I had better close about here. I hope mother and David are doing fine in their
studying and homework and that all else is going good back home. Keep counting the days with me, bye for now.

                    Your son,

                         Mike

P.S.
     If you wrote since we last talked on the phone I'll probably get it in the morning before we leave and will answer when we get back in.

1968-10-27.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-10-27.text:
Sunday 27 Oct.

Dear Mother, Dad + David,

     Friday evening I received your letter after I got back to the ship. I've got another week behind me and a three day weekend to look forward to this week. Last week was pretty hectic and much the same routine we have at sea.
     We were suppose to be back in about 2 PM Friday but didn't moor until 7:30 that night. The fog was so heavy they had trouble navigating in the harbor so sat it out for a while and when we did start in it was a long affair.
This other FT and myself operate our radar for navigation when we come in to port. We got a "well done" from one of the officers because of the job we did on tracking contacts in the fog on our way in.
     I have duty today and its about 9 AM here. I suppose I'll watch the football game around 10.
     Last night I went to the arena and saw a hockey game. San Diego won and it was a good one. I am going again Tuesday night when they play Seattle.
     Yesterday I spent some more money as I have been doing on Saturdays for the past couple of weeks. I have got about all of the clothes I want and about all I need to get now are a few uniform accessories like rating badges and a neckerchief.
     I have enough things to send another box home now and may send it sometime this week or next.
     I am almost certain I'll be home anywhere from the 15th to 18th. Of course I don't know for sure but this
seems to be the procedure they are following. So I have less than three weeks left and only two weeks to get ready because that last week I want to have it done.
     We are not due to get underway again until Nov. 19th but there is rumor out that the captain has voluntered us to run plane guard for one of the carriers the week of the 4th. We should find out for sure about that this week. Believe me the things that happen here on this ship really do
make a lot of people mad. There were really a lot of angry wifes and families Friday night after being 5½ hours late. And the week before that, we were going to moor at pier 6. All the people were there waiting for the ship and as the ship neared the pier we backed down and went all the way down to pier 2. Again there were some angry people. The reason for this stunt they say is that the water wasn't deep enough at pier 6 so we had to moor at pier 2. All I can say is, in three weeks it will be over
with (I hope).
     I'm glad to hear about the job promotion for Dad, hope he likes it. No doubt this may be a little incentive to trade for a new car. I was reading in those clippings about the carpenters picketing at the hospital because of a dispute over some doors. I bet there is a good story behind that one. Also I noticed the write-up about the Chicago Bears possibly coming to town. All I can say is it will never happen. What do they plan on doing, build a 30,000 seat stadium then
charge $10 a head to see it. Maybe they could arrange to play on MacArthur's football field and give the proceeds to the school board as an act of charity. The whole idea sounds ridiculous.
     Of course, if all goes well, I'll spend this coming weekend at Georgia Mae's. This should be the last weekend I have up there and I will be sending some things home from there.
     Well its about time for the football game to start so I had better go here. David, be good and study hard in
school. See you soon.

                    your son,

                         Mike

1968-10-30.label: Mike Ducy to Home
1968-10-30.text:
Oct. 30, 1968
Wednesday, 1620

Dear Mother, Dad, and David,

     Only one more day is left in this month then it is November. This has been a slow month for me but I am sure those first two weeks of next month will go by fast.
     This morning I received your letter of the 26th. The pictures were good and the newspaper clipping was informative as usual.
     I also got a letter from Bill today that he wrote the 18th. He typed it and made very few errors with the exception of his spell-
ing which seems to be a trademark of his. But it was very neat and I was glad to see that he has the incentive to type.
     I'll be calling Georgia Mae around 7:30 PM tonight and see if I can visit them this weekend. I am ready for a few days away from here and really do look forward to going up there.
     Last night one of the other FT's and I went out to the arena and saw the Gulls play hockey. It was a pretty rough and wild game but ended in a 2-2 tie.
     Although I don't have duty tonight I plan on staying aboard instead of going into town. I seem to have been caught a little short on finances this week after my shopping spree of Saturday. I will probably go over on the base to the movie about 8:30 to occupy the rest of the evening.
     I was sorry to hear about David hurting his leg. I hope it hasn't became too serious and isn't bothering him now. No doubt he is anxious for tomorrow night to get here so he can go
trick-or-treating.
     I hope you can sign me up for that test and that I'll be able to take it when I get home. It sounds like a good job and I'd like the opportunity to give it a try.
     We had a little rain late last night while I was returning to the ship. This is no doubt a sign that winter isn't too far away. But I doubt if there will be the rain like we had last winter. Of course now that we are back on standard time it really does seem like winter is near.
     Monday I went
through a physical exam to see if I am healthy enough to get out of here and be turned loose as a civilian. This is one of the many steps you have to go through to get your freedom but is usually where they start. As I think of it thats one of the first things they do when they bring you in this outfit. So I guess it works both ways. In case you are wondering about my foot I am glad to say that it has healed completely and isn't causing me a bit of trouble. The corpsman didn't ask to look at it
but did ask me how it was so I told him and he seemed convinced.
     Well I guess I'll close here and write to Bill. Bye for now. Hope to see you soon.

                    Your son,

                         Mike

1968-05-24.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-05-24.text:
24 May, 68
Hoi An

[Written on stationery with printed map of Vietnam]

Mike,

I got your letter yesterday, boy you squids are finely getting to see some action.

Yea I remember that guy you told me about. He must of really been fucked in the mind.

I'll be sending you some slides and a tape for on there around the 10th of June so be looking for them. — Have you gotten that one tape yet?

Boy we had some more hell here again the other night. There were fire fights all over the place. We were lucky only 5 rounds come up our way. It all lasted about on 1½ hours.

Today I was messing with a blasting cap from a gook dud. I threw it on a fire and started to take off. Well I got hit 23 times with shrapnel in the right arm and chest. I dug it all out and put some shit on it to help heal it up. I guess I wont try that again.

I got a letter from Jim Dick yesterday too. He's up at Phu Bai at an ammo dump. He seems to be doing a lot of skating.

Some ass hole Major was up here today to look over the place. He said we live like pigs and don't even act like Marines. So now we have to hold muster at 0730 every morning, and can't fuck off like we did before. All of us are really pissed off about that 0730 deal.

It got up to 107° the 20th. and it was a hot S.O.B.

Well son going to go for now, be good and don't fall off of your tub. See you later.

"Little Brother"
Bill

"THEY CAN FUCK WITH ME ALL THEY WANT BUT THEY CAN'T STOP THE CLOCK." 276 days left in Nam & 15 months left in the Corps. I AM GETTING SHORT! HAHA.

1968-05-27.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-05-27.text:
Dear Mike,

Here the pictures and the speed and type of recorder "3 3/4 I.P.S." "MONO"

Be looking for a tape from you real soon too.

Little Brother
Bill USMC.

1968-06-21.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-06-21.text:
21 June 68
Da Nang

Mike,

Sounds as if you poor squids had a little action up your way. Just make sure you get those MIG pilots back safe and fuck the others (ha ha.)

Here is that money order for the 30 bucks I owe you. I finely got to a post office to get it made out.

Now Sam is in Da Nang back at the Bn. area. I am on 30 days of mess duty, and Sam really skating. I have the mid duty, and all of my work is done by 8:30 PM. I can't really bitch because no one fucks with me, and the one thing I can't stand is to get fucked with.

Do you remember that Bob White me and Carter, Angle and Penny hung around with and drank together? Well I saw him in Hoi-An, his in the Seabees. He gave me a Allied catalog. I am going to order a Sony 907 tape recorder, it only cost $34.50. I also checked at the PX for one and it cost $31.00 but would take 3-4 months to get to me. So I said fuck that! What do you think about it? OK ya you know that walkie-talkie we bought (C-555) well they've got them for $11.00 now each. If you want to look at this catalog I'll send it. Just let me know.

Well I am going to go for now, I'll write again soon. Be good and don't "fall off the ship."

P.S. I almost forgot               Little Brother
Connie wanted your                  Bill
address, so I gave it to her.
Has she written yet? Just wondering.
                                    OVER

1968-07-13.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-07-13.text:
13 July 68
Da Nang

Mike,

I got your tape yesterday and really enjoyed it.

I'm glad to hear you think that this tape recorder will be a good buy. I didn't really want an one for A.C. power only because of the power change over here. And I can always get a hold of batteries for it.

I also got those slides you took, they were really good. You said in your tape that the chopper got their ass's kicked when they went in land. Boy I bet those chopper guys were really shitting their skivvies when the V.C. started giving them hell.

You should be back in the states by the time you get this letter you lucky fucker. Now I've got only 226 more days left over here. And have been here for 167 days.

I asked for 30 more days of mess duty, this mess duty is really skating and the time goes by fast.

We've had 2 "red alerts" last week but nothing has come of them. Rockets were spotted taking off but they weren't coming our way. They hit the air strip and Marble Mt. about 5 miles away.

This morning at 4 AM while we were going to pick up the gooks that work in our mess hall the jeep driver fell asleep and ran off the road down a 50 ft. embankment. The 2 guys in the jeep wasn't hurt, but sure had the shit scared out of them.

Its been fairly quiet around here the past few nites, but we are expecting to be hit soon.

I'll be getting a tape made and sent off to you soon.

Well thats about all from over here in Nam, I keep you informed if anything big comes up. You know like pulling all the U.S. Troops out or something like that. ha ha!

Bye for now and take care.

Little Brother
Bill USMC.

1968-08-01.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-08-01.text:
1 Aug. 68
Da Nang

Mike,

I got that tape and really enjoyed it a lot. By the way do you still have your little Sony? If so I'll send G.M. a tape real soon.

I got paid again today, and this makes my 9th month as P.F.C. I wish they'd get their shit together and promote me.

Now man listen to this, a little paper we get over here 2 times a month had a little article in it. It said anyone who has less than 6 mo. left in the Corps when they return from Nam get out early. So if I'm lucky I'll get out in 15 mos instead of 24. Sorry you squids don't get it. (ha ha ha)

Its been fairly quiet the past week over here. But we did have 2 V.C. firing in at us one nite, so every one was in the trenches then the word was passed "FREE FIRE" so me and the cooks I work with opened up on where they was at. I fired 36 rounds in a 15 yd. area where the firing was coming from. So if those V.C. were still there they probly got their ass blown off or the shit scared out of them.

Well I've got only 18 more days left on mess duty. I am trying to get on patrols as a radio man. They said if there was an opening when I got off mess duty I could get on.

And I am going to try and take my R&R either Oct or Nov. I don't know where I want to go for sure yet.

In another 4 days I'll have been in Nam for 6 mos., the time sure has flown for me. I got only 207 more days left over here in this hole.

Oh yea day before yesterday when had a flame tank down here burning the weeds from the barb wire, they caught some of the gooks huts on fire. Which I thought was real funny, I also got some good flicks of it too.

Well as you said all the girls in Cal. look good to you, I just hope they stay that way when I got back to the "big USA."

Its still good and hot over here and it seems to keep getting hotter every day. Also the liberty still sucks, you know I like not at all. Be looking for a tape and some slides heading your way from me soon.

Well I guess I'll be going for now. Write again soon.

Little Brother
Bill

P.S. "SEE THE
BAL LIBERTY SPOTS
JOIN THE CORPS"

1968-09-25.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-09-25.text:
Sept. 25, 68
Da Nang

Mike,

I got your letter you wrote the 19th today.

Well things with the Corps is same as before, "they suck."

Boy I guess you are really short, but there isn't much I can say about it but 151 days left over here. and hopping the same for the Corps.

I checked on my R&R and that ass hole SSgt. forgot to put my name down for it. So now I've got to wait till Nov. instead of Oct.

We just had a red alert, 2 rounds come busten balls over our heads. They didn't hit anywhere around that we could tell. Now all the "boots" that think their "salty" are telling sea storys. What a laugh!

I put in for my L/cpl. test today, and should be takin it soon.

I am also signed the pay roster, for $73.00 and sending $100.00 to the bank.

Sounds as if your liberty is starting to be fucked up. To bad squid, we don't get any over here.

I am going to be sending some books on Scott amps. see what you think about them. and which one will be the best cheapest ones. Then send me back your ideas, and then I'll order them.

Well I guess I'd best be goin for now. Write when ever you can, and I'll do the same.

Bye for now, and take care

Little Brother
Bill

P.S. I got my $100.00 from the State today. Have you got yours yet?

1968-11-03.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-11-03.text:
Nov. 3, 68
Da Nang

Mike,

Well here I am again, in the big "rat hole" Nam.

I can't remember if I told you or not, but I am on patrols for 60 days. I've only been out once at night and tonight will be my 2nd time.

Its not really to bad out there, but it does get kind of scary. you know? The other nite once when we was out the A.R.V.N.'s opened up on us from the other side of the river, we got down for awhile, then up. They fired again and we got down then we moved out and was fired at again but kept going. 3 guys got down and we didn't know it. after we went about 150 ft. we found out they wasn't with us. So we hit our rifle stocks to let them know we were looking for them. The point there I found him in some brush and something moved so he opened up on it then threw a frag. at it, after that the 3 guys started yelling at us. and they were really pissed off at the point. after that happened we come back into the C.A. We was out twice that nite from 7:PM - 11:PM and 2:AM - 5:30 AM. boy

was I tired when we got in.

Jim Dick was out to see me this morning, but I had to leave about ½ hour after he got here. I plan on seeing him again tomorrow on my day off.

Well have the big short timer doing? In 112 more days I'll be on my way home too. and in 25 days I'll be going on R&R to Taipei for 5 fun filled days of booze & pussy!

Well thats about it for now, hope to hear from you soon. Bye for now & take care.

Little Brother
Bill USMC

1968-11-26.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-11-26.text:
Nov. 26, 68
Da Nang

Mike,

Well here I am again, sorry for taking so long. But I was going to wait till you got home.

I am still on patrols and doing alright. Yesterday the patrol got hit by 3 V.C., only one guy got hurt by a grenade that was thrown at them by the gooks. I went out that night too, but it was at a later time and in a different area. also there was only 5 of us, I was walking drag man but our radio-man got sick so we couldn't set up any good ambushes. So we brought him in and I took over the radio for the rest of the night. We was delayed going out about 1½ hrs. because we had 2 red alerts in about a 3 hrs. Boy the lifers were sure sweating it.

Oh yea, I had my "shipping over" lecture last week! Man all the things bennies they'll give me after 20 yrs. all I said was "I am not interested." and - also passed my G.E.D. test, now all I've got to do is write Mac. and send them my score. I am really happy about it.

In 4 more days I'll be on R&R, I am really going to live it up for those 5 days.

In about 90 days I'll be on my way home. I guess I could say I'm SHORT!, since I started out with 393 days. and time really has flown for me, last year at this time I was home on leave.

Now tell me how the big town doing? Have you started looking for a job yet?

Well I guess I'll be going for now, take care, and watch yourself with those Decatur girls. ha ha. Bye for now.

"U.S.M.C.                          Little Brother
 NEVER AGAIN"                      Bill

1968-12-08.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-12-08.text:
Dec. 8, 68
Da Nang

Mike,

Well I am back from my R&R. and let me tell you I really had a wonderful time. and would like to go back, but I doubt I will. and those girls there really were fine, if you know what I mean.

Yea, I'd sure like to see your new car, it sounds like a mover.

Talking about shot guns, would you take and oil mine down real good for me? Its been a little over a year for it. David should be able to show you some good hunting places.

Yea I am still on patrols, last night we was out in a 7 man-ambush. I was set up in some brush along this trail when I heard some movement comming my way. Well I threw a hand illum, and lite up that area, I spotted something trying to move out, I fired about 10 rounds at it. We then broke the ambush and checked out the area, all we found was a little blood. So I guess he was hit.

Today we had a USO show, and was it bad. They had guts to be on that stage.

Now tell me how big Decatur is doing? I bet its still dead as usual.

Well now only 77 more days left over here in this hell hole! I just hope days go by fast, like the 316 before have done.

Thats about it for now, write when ever you can and good luck in getting a job.

Little Brother
Bill

P.S. 1 more day and I'll be 19 years old. Wow. B.F.D.

SHORT!

1968-12-20.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1968-12-20.text:
Dec. 20, 68
Da Nang

Mike,

Well here I am again, and still going strong.

Your job sounds like it might be something good. What are the chances for raises for you. $100.00 a week ain't bad for starting out.

Well in 11 more days I going to be requesting mast for Lance/cpl. I think 13 months in grade is too much, and I could sure use the $20.00 extra.

The action around here has been picking up a little. Last night about 8:30 the ARVN's down at the bottom of our hill caught 2 V.C. in a ville about 50 meters from our C.P. They had a radio listening to a V.C. broadcast. They took them in and their small camp for questioning. Talk about the ways they have to make the V.C. talk. 1st they beat the shit out of them with bamboo sticks, then put them in a small barb-wire pen about 2½ ft in Dim. and about a foot high. While in there the V.C. were being poked with the sticks. Well all in all they spilt the beans about what was happening around the Da Nang area. One thing they said was there is 51 V.C. in our near area. One kid was 16 and the other was 17, at first I felt sorry for them, but they sure wouldn't feel that way for us if they popped us off. So when we took it slow and easy down the trail, in about 50 yds. we found a boobie trap. Luckly they weren't armed yet. The C.O.C. bunker told us to forget our main mission, and to set up an ambush at the edge of this ville. So we set there for 5 hrs., but didn't see anything but a dog, but we cut him a hurr and didn't blow him away.

I've been carrying a 12 ga. shotgun, (which holds 6 rounds) on the day patrols mostly to kill snakes with. I got 3 yesterday while crossing a paddy. I'll start carrying it at nights while walking dogs when they get me some OO buck, now all they've got is #4 buck. I don't like it at night cause the pattern is so big.

Well I've got only 65 more days left over here in the Nam. And have been here for 328 days. I just hope the time keeps flyin by.

I'd best be goin for now, I've got to get up early for the morning patrol. So bye for now, take care and good luck in your job.

Little Brother
Bill

"SHORT"

1969-02-06.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1969-02-06.text:
Feb. 6, 69
Da Nang

Mike,

Well here I am again and doing fine. Haven't heard from you for a while.

Now I've got only 13 days left over here in Nam. My flight date for the states is the 20th. of this month. I should be home around the 27th. And when I get home let me tell you we're really going to raise hell in that town.

I got my sea bag packed and ready to mail home, and sold some of my gear to the boots that just got in.

I bought a $53.00 suit case at the P.X. for only $30.50 and its really a dandy. I just can't see carrying that sea bag with me home and mailing it is real cheap.

I am off patrols now and back in the co. area. They've got me mostly on working party's and duty driver.

It turned off cold the past few days. It wasn't really cold, but down in the 60's is cold as for over here, and we froze our ass's off.

Well I'd best be going for now, see you soon and take care.

                           Little Brother
P.S. SHORT                 Bill

1969-02-18.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1969-02-18.text:
Feb. 18, 69
Da Nang

Mike,

Well here I am again and short as ever. Only 2 more big days and I'll be out of this fucked-up place for good. I'll be on my big freedom bird the 20th.

I plan on staying out at G.M.'s for about 2 days then head on home. I just hope you'll still be in Decatur at least till I get off of leave.

I've got my boot camp I.D. in here and want you to keep it for me. I told the Co. office that I lost it so I could get a new one with my mustach on it.

your place no. is a real good one and easy to remember.

They sure have been fucking with us short timers here at 7th Comm. I was on bunkers last week & now I'm on assit. duty N.C.O. from 12 midnight to 6:30 AM. But one good thing about it they can't stop the clock. Its now 2:45 AM & about 10 hrs. from now I'll be checking out of this chicken shit Bn. for good.

Well I'd best be going for now, see you soon & take care.

Little Brother
Bill

P.S. NOT SHORT -
NEXT!

1969-04-15.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1969-04-15.text:
April 15, 69

Mike,

Well here I am, boy does this place really suck. About the only thing to do around here is drink or take off for the weekend and go about 350 miles to have a good time.

That wasn't to bad on the car, just if it runs better and doesn't leak oil I can get a real good watch for you for $30.29 and a ball from 16.50 - $22.00 shoes are $0.25 and bag is $5.25.

If you could get your hand sized at one of the lanes I think it would fit you better. I've been doing alot of bowling this past week, the highest I've gotten was 194.

Well payday come for us tomorrow, I hope to get about $60.00.

I've been buying alot of record alb's. They're only $2.90 for the $4.70 reg.

That tax refund wasn't much, I'll cash it tomorrow with my other check.

I've got duty this weekend so I won't be leaving this place until next week.

I got in a welding class about 6 miles from base. It cost me $16.00 for 11 weeks, which I go 2 nights a week for 3 hrs. each night. Plus I got 2 books, one on arc welding and the other on blue print reading for welding. I sure hope to do good in it.

Boy I'm glad that I'm getting that cut, they've been getting guys that have more time than me to go to get on a ship for 3½ mo. to Greece and other places. They've got 5 from my section.

Well I guess thats about all the news for now, so take care. Oh, yea could you look up Linda's address and send it to me?

See you soon.

                           Little Brother
P.S. Last but                Bill
not least I've
been running 3
miles a day to get
in shape and lose some
weight.

1969-04-27.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1969-04-27.text:
4/27/69

Mike,

I got your letter last Wednesday with the check in it. I picked up your watch that day. I also got a twist-o-flex of band for it. It was a $6.00 band for only $3.00.

I guess you know by now that I'm getting out the 1st of June, but it'll really be on the 2nd since the 1st is on a Monday. But anyway I'm getting out. 35 days to go!

I sent off a letter to that co. in Mon about my sunglasses the 24th, its really pissed me off not getting them yet.

We've been having really good weather this past week. I layed out in the sun for about 2 hrs. today and got a little red.

Me and a buddy of mine went down to the local skeet range to shoot. Boy those throwers they've got really send those clay pig. out fast. The guy that runs the place said they leave the trap going 65 MPH. and I believe it. It only cost $1.70 for the shells & birds. Which ain't to bad.

Also last night I went bowling and got a 252 score on one game. and the total of 3 games was 557. I was really happy with that 252.

Well I'd best be going for now, its almost 10:00 PM and lights go out then. So take care.

SHORT                          Little Brother
                               Bill

1969-05-20.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1969-05-20.text:
20 MAY 69

Mike,

Well here I am again.
I've started checking out of the USMC. Boy I can hardly waite til I get out.

Here is the list of records that I've got. Most of them are $2.90 and a couple $3.40, cause they've a poster in them.

Well hows your new job doing? I hope fine.

I've only got 3 more welding classes left, then I'll be set for some good money.

Hey could you ask Jackie to check on Linda and find out why she haint written yet?

I've been going up to Maryland the past 2 weekends with a buddy, and have really been having some fun. He's got a 3,000.00 basement turned into a party room like. And we really get drunk.

Well thats about all thats new, see you in 2 weeks.

Little Brother
Bill

1969-10-18.label: Bill Ducy to Mike
1969-10-18.text:
Oct. 18, 69
Da Nang

Mike,

Well here Iam again, I got your letter about 3 days ago. Now Ive finely got time to write back.

How do you like this typewritter? Well Ibought it off a guy for $45. Its not a bad deal, its a Royal.

Guess what, Jim Dick was down to see me, hes now in Da Nang for duty about ½ mile from me at an ammo dump. We plan on meeting at the 327 PX Sun. for a few beers and some sea stories.

Its been raining like a son-of a-bitch the past 6 days. everything is wet and fucked up.

I got wiped out of my mind last night, boy that beer can really fuck you up fast if you havent had any for awhile. If you know what I mean.

I guess you are getting short, I just hope I can get that 6mo. cut when I leve here in Feb.

Yes, I can get thoes Jap. recorders at the PX, but they sell fast, but if Iam lucky I can get ahold of one. Iam getting some real good tapes off a buddy of mine in a few days. Ill send them home so they dont get fucked-up or swiped.

When am I going to make L/cpl? Well Id like to know to. Ive got areal good chance Nov. because they are going by time in grade instead of all that other bull-shit.

Well Id best be goin for now, take care and dont fuck all that pussy!!!!! 128 more days left over here.

Little Brother
Bill
Bill

PS. U.S.M.C.=
U.nesserry
S.hit &
M.assive
C.onfusion

1968-06-20.label: WF Given to Mike
1968-06-20.text:
Thurs. 20 Jun

Greetings Duc,
        Well ol' buddy whats it like
in the real Navy?
        I haven't heard from you
recently so I decided to write.
We just finished up making river
supply runs. We now are on market
time patrol. You may know exactly
what I'm talking about. In case
you don't - I explain a little.
  We carry ammo, fuel, and spare
parts along with a spare crew
for 4 swift boats. Once each
day, each boat, comes alongside
for a spare crew and re-supply.
You've read enough about swifts
to know they check all junks
and watch the coast line.
     Well ol' buddy do you
remember in school when we were
told about type desks. I wrote
to the Ft Branch and to a
senator about wanting a one year
tour because I'm married.
  Guess what - I am leaving here
in Sept for 30 days leave and
then reporting to the USS
Tulare AKA 112. It has 6-3"50's
and quite a bit of FT gear -
I have a lot to learn before
I get there.

#2

  I've been searching for info
on 3" mounts but no luck so far.
I hope they have patience with
me. Maybe I can learn
some electronics while I'm
there.
     Well are you going for
second class this fall? I
think I'll take the test but
if I do pass I'm not extending
for second.               (in Navy)
     Well I'm over 3 now, celebrated
my 20th birthday, 1st anniversary
and decided the Navy's not
for me - how about you. I've
been getting nothing but
screwed over. We have had
laundry or fresh water showers
since we left Taiwan. I've
spent so much time on watch
on this thing - I almost
live in the pilot house or
after-steering.
     Well not much else is
happening. I don't have any
Purple Heart or Navy Cross
yet. We've got the
usual 3 ribbons & we're up
for unit citation.

#3.

  My new ship is out of Diego
so maybe I'll see you.
Just think Duc - pretty
soon we're half way.

  Well I best go.

            Take care & write,
                   Sincerely
                     Giv

P.S. Plan to be in Subic from
3 July to 25th then Guam
for 5 weeks just in case
you are

1969-01-06.label: AR Norris to Mike
1969-01-06.text:
6 Jan. 1969

Dear Mike,

    HAPPY NEW YEAR !! Thanks for the letter , we were all glad to hear from you. Glad to hear you got the cruise book alright..What did you think of it? I thought there was going to be more colored pictures. It's good to see you got right in the swing of things getting a job so soon and buying a car && right off.

(Excuse my typing but I never was very good)

    I reported back from leave this morning and it sure was great to get off this boat for awhile. We had a very beautiful Christmas  and New Year's. It sure was nice to be with the family and relatives over the holidays. Meadows had duty New Year's eve ha! ha! Ole was home in ILL. for the holidays and now he's got a touch of the H.K. flu. Underwood ?? what can I say! The jolly J. is still the same. As a matter of fact , we have a material inspection this friday 11 th.
